# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, us…
Let me read the input files for the PR review.

But there is a subtle issue: `providerTuningBootNotices()` resolves by name, which looks up `forName(name)` — the FIRST entry with that name. For entries whose `forName` resolves to a DIFFERENT entry (e.g. same name in two lanes — customProviders `x` vs role ref named `role:x/model`? no those are prefixed)... Names: customProviders → raw name; models.custom → `models.custom.<key>`; roles → `role:<label>`; queue → `queue:<label>`. All lanes are namespaced except customProviders, which is unique per registry. So duplicates are unlikely. This was flagged in r2 (duplicate name across lanes prints first entry's values) and addressed via namespacing? Actually the r2 reply said the fix was longest-base-path-wins forUrl; the boot-notice duplicate-name issue was mentioned in r2 review as "Same root cause, smaller blast radius". If two entries have the same name (possible? register() replaces per (name, baseUrl) — so same name with DIFFERENT baseUrls can coexist! e.g. two customProviders entries can't share a name in the registry... but two role refs with the same label? ModelRef.label = 'provider/modelId'. A roles chain can contain the same provider/modelId twice? Possibly. Or a queue entry and role ref with the same label? Queue uses `queue:` prefix and role uses `role:` prefix, so no cross-lane. Within-lane duplicates: customProviders — registry likely enforces unique names. models.custom — map keys unique. roleRefs — a chain could legitimately contain duplicates (e.g. a fallback chain with the same provider/model listed twice? unusual). queue — labels probably unique.

Actually, wait, more subtle: `forName` returns the FIRST entry with that name; for two entries with same name but different baseUrls and different overrides, the boot notice for the second entry would print the first entry's values. Edge case, low probability. r2 already noted this as "smaller blast radius" and it wasn't explicitly fixed — the fix was precedence. Hmm, but did r2 consider it fixed? The author's reply addressed forUrl precedence. The notice resolution by name remains. This is a minor edge; at most a SUGGESTION.

3. `resolveProviderTimeouts(name: ...)` — when resolving by name, if the entry's overrides are partial (e.g. only streamIdle), the connect leg falls to global. And `sourceName: entry?.name` is set even when neither field came from the entry — e.g. entry has only connect override, streamIdle comes from global → `streamIdleSource: globalOverride` but `sourceName` is entry.name — fine, label for global is 'global' ignoring sourceName. OK.

But wait — `describe()` uses `connectSource.label(sourceName)` — for `providerEntry` label is `provider:$entryName`. OK.

4. In `forUrl`, precedence: `>=` with `_baseDepth`. Note `_matchesBaseUrl` requires scheme+host+port match. Fine.

One issue: `register()` removes entries per (name, baseUrl) then appends. `forUrl` last-wins for equal depth. Boot order: config pass then queue pass. OK.

5. `parseProviderTimeoutMs` — `value is! int` — yaml `connectTimeoutMs: 1.5` would be a double → error. Good. But note `node['connectTimeoutMs']` on a yaml map returns yaml scalar; YamlNode wrapped ints — in Dart's yaml package, `node['key']` on YamlMap returns the scalar value (int) directly for map access? YamlMap is a Map view that unwraps scalars. Yes, YamlMap implements Map<dynamic, dynamic> with unwrapped values. But `parseProviderTimeoutMs` is called with `node['connectTimeoutMs']` where node is `Map<Object?, Object?>` — in models_config, node is YamlMap. Values are unwrapped ints. OK.

`parseProviderTimeoutMs` has a weird line: `// ignore: avoid_dynamic_calls final value = node;` — node is `Object?`, so `value` is just node; no dynamic calls at all. The ignore comment is pointless but harmless. Actually wait — it's declared `Object? node`, so `value` is `Object?`. `avoid_dynamic_calls` lint wouldn't fire. Harmless noise, SUGGESTION at most.

6. The `_sendWatchedOnce` change: the timeout error message now uses the resolved `connectTimeout` — good.

7. `createSseIterator`: `idleTimeout ?? _tunedIdleTimeout(response)` — explicit param wins. `_tunedIdleTimeout` reads `response.request?.url`. In tests with MockClient, `request` is set. In real http, StreamedResponse.request is set when passed. OK. Note: the redirect case — response.request is the final request. OK.

8. Boot: `seedProviderTuning(roleRefs: [...])` — flattens all role chains. ModelRef with no baseUrl is skipped in the adapter. Good.

9. Boot notices captured AFTER queue pass. Fixed as claimed. Pinned with tests (need to verify).

10. The new commit 1cf19f60f split the seeder into table-driven adapters. Behavior "identical"? Let me compare with the previous version to be sure. The claim: entries without overrides never reach the table — via `registerAll` → `register` → `entry.isEmpty` return. And `.nonNulls` filters null adapters for role/queue refs with no baseUrl. Previously (e68b6750e), what did it look like? Let me check git show e68b6750e:lib/src/cli/provider_tuning_seed.dart to verify behavior identical.

Let me grep for toYaml usage. This is a breaking change for external consumers of the barrel export. It's fine internally (covariant assignment would break callers who do `Map<String, String> m = entry.toYaml()`). Let me check usages.

11. `mergeEditedCustomProviderEntry` — in edit mode the wizard no longer carries `authMethod` inline; it applies merge. Wait — previous code had `authMethod: existingEntry?.authMethod ?? CustomProviderAuthMethod.apiKey` in the constructor. But when existingEntry == null (new entry), authMethod = apiKey default, authHeader = null. Same as before. In edit mode, previously authHeader was NOT carried (r2 flagged this), now it is. Good.

But wait — there's a subtlety: in the rename path above (`registry.entries.removeWhere((e) => e.name == editName)`), editName differs from setup.name. The merge uses existingEntry — fine.

12. Barrel: two export lines appended within existing groups. Per gh-1232: "GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, exports sorted by path within a group". `export 'src/cli/provider_tuning_seed.dart';` was appended after `env_provider_preconfig.dart` — is that sorted? Within the cli group: browser_bridge_commands, custom_providers, key_status, env_provider_preconfig, provider_tuning_seed, model_roles/provider_key_resolver... Hmm, the ordering looks like NOT strictly sorted alphabetically already (key_status before env_provider_preconfig?). The policy says sorted by path within a group, but the existing list isn't sorted anyway. Append-only is respected. Fine.

a) `providerTuningBootNotices()` resolution-by-name vs by-URL inconsistency: the notice for entry E resolves values via `forName(E.name)`. Suppose two same-name entries (role chain listing the same provider twice with different overrides, or two queue entries with the same label). The second's notice prints the first's values. Minor.

More interesting: `resolveProviderTimeouts(name: entry.name)` → `forName` returns the FIRST entry with that name — which may not be `entry` itself. For distinct names it's fine.

b) In `resolveProviderTimeouts`, when `name` is given but no entry matches, it falls to `url == null ? null : forUrl(url)` — but providerTuningBootNotices passes only name. OK.

c) AC6 claim: "empty registry short-circuits to the untouched effective getters". `providerConnectTimeoutForUrl` checks `providerTuningRegistry.isEmpty` first. Behavior identical when empty... except `response.request?.url == null` → also effective. Good.

Hmm, but `int.tryParse` on huge numbers like "999" returns null → malformed. Fine.

On a hot stream path (per chunk!), that's O(n) memmove per chunk — 2048-element shift per chunk. For thousands of chunks that's fine-ish in practice (2048 pointer moves ~ microseconds), but the review r2 suggestion said ring buffer; the author chose drop-oldest with removeAt(0). Hmm — "All methods are cheap (append + counter) and safe to call from stream paths" — the doc claims cheap; removeAt(0) is O(n) with n up to 2048. Per-chunk cost of moving 2048 pointers is ~2μs. Negligible vs network chunk processing. I'll leave a SUGGESTION-level nit maybe. Actually let me not manufacture nits; but the doc statement "All methods are cheap (append + counter)" is slightly inaccurate once the window is full (append + O(n) shift). It's still cheap in absolute terms. I might mention it briefly as a suggestion.

i) `_humanize`: for `d.inMilliseconds % 1000 != 0` → tenths. E.g. 1500ms → 15 → tenths = 1.5 → '1.5s'. Good. For 400ms → tenths = 4.0 → '4s'. Good. For 3650000ms (60.83min)? inSeconds=3650 → '3650s'. Fine.

j) `_matchesBaseUrl`: URL with default port omitted — handled via _defaultPort. Non-http(s) schemes (e.g. ws) → base port null vs url port null → equal. OK.

Case: baseUrl with path '/' → basePath empty → matches any path on host. Fine.

k) Now the seeding sources: `saved.customProviders` — is that the full list from config? `CliConfig.customProviders`? And models: `saved.models?.custom`. And roleRefs from `saved.modelRoles?.roles.values`. What about `envProviderPreconfig` or other lanes? Out of scope.

In this codebase, `CliIO.write` = primary stream, `writeln` = diagnostics. The queue notices also use... let me check how queueNotices are printed — `for (final notice in queueNotices) { ... }` — need to look. In the diff, tuning notices use io.writeln right before queueNotices loop. Let me check what queueNotices uses. If queue notices use io.writeln too, consistent.

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review…

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, us…
Let me read the input files for the PR review.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1400
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1400
- **Title**: feat(1398): stall-recovery tuning from the references — per-provider idle timeouts, server-advertised backoff, dual retry budgets
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `feat/1398-stall-recovery-tuning` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 15
- **Additions**: +2367
- **Deletions**: -13
- **Created**: 2026-10-07T23:07:20Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-08T01:06:33Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1398

One sentence: the stall-recovery knobs become per-provider and data-driven — idle/connect timeout, backoff source, and retry budgets resolve per provider entry instead of one global constant, with the tuning recipe computed from measured inter-chunk gaps.

## Delivered vs remaining (AC table)

| AC | status | where |
|---|---|---|
| **AC1** per-provider timeout overrides | ✅ delivered | `providerTuningRegistry` + `resolveProviderTimeouts` (`lib/src/providers/provider_tuning.dart`): entry > `providerTimeouts:` global > 180s/300s defaults, per field. Parsed from `customProviders:`, `models.custom:`, roles chain entries, `providersQueue:` entries (strict positive-int ms). IT: `provider_tuning_loopback_test.dart` — a registered `streamIdleTimeoutMs: 1500` entry fires the idle watchdog at ~1.5s on a real loopback silent stream while an unregistered host keeps the default; the adapter-level UT proves `streamOpenAICompletions` inherits it end-to-end. Boot notices print every seeded entry's effective values (sources labeled `provider:<name>`/`global`/`default`). |
| **AC2** server-advertised backoff | ✅ contract delivered | `resolveRetryBackoff`: parseable delta-seconds `Retry-After` wins for that attempt, hard ceiling 60s with a named clamp (`Retry-After: 300` → 60s + the advertised value on the trace); E2 `0` → absent; E3 malformed/HTTP-date → ladder + note. UT fake-clock suite green. |
| **AC3** dual retry budgets | ✅ delivered | `RetryBudgetLedger`: connection cap 4 / stream cap 3, fully independent counters; UT + IT (five connect-class kills exhaust connection only, the subsequent idle-class stall draws the untouched stream budget; E5 terminal story carries both counts). |
| **AC4** trace format contract | ✅ delivered | `formatRetryTraceLine` — `budget=<connection|stream> attempt=<n>/<cap> delay=<ladder:10s|server:12s|clamp:60s>` + clamp/malformed annotations; format-contract UT pins it. |
| **AC5** data-driven tuning report | ✅ report/seam half | `InterChunkGapRecorder` (per-model p50/p95 nearest-rank + watchdog fires) + `renderTuningReport` with the `streamIdleTimeoutMs ≈ 2× p95` recipe line; empty recorder renders nothing (AC5's "when instrumentation data is present"). **Remaining:** the production feeder is #1392's LatencyMeter + the idle-fire sites — the card names them as the sources; this PR lands the report + the seam they feed. |
| **AC6** REG: byte-identical when untuned | ✅ delivered | empty registry short-circuits to the untouched effective getters; the full `test/providers` suite (660 tests incl. the transient-retry, sse-idle, connect-stall, real-client-watchdog REGs), `test/config` + `cli_config_test` (272), `test/model_roles` (233), `test/parity` (32), hosts + agent-loop + bin-wiring suites all green. |

Edge cases: E1 pinned (defaults stay 300s; codex's 5s explicitly NOT adopted), E2/E3 covered above, E4 the table is read per request so a re-seed applies to the NEXT request while in-flight requests keep theirs, E5 covered.

## Territory note (three lanes in provider files)

New files own everything: `lib/src/providers/provider_tuning.dart`, `lib/src/cli/provider_tuning_seed.dart`, and the three test files. Shared-file surface (all additive, no restructuring):
- `provider_common.dart` — **two minimal additive value-read hunks** (the exact allowance this lane was granted): `_sendWatchedOnce` resolves the connect budget via `providerConnectTimeoutForUrl(request.url)`; `createSseIterator`'s default idle value via `_tunedIdleTimeout(response)` (explicit `idleTimeout` params still win — #1392's watchdog wiring and env plumbing untouched; empty registry returns today's exact values).
- Config parsers (`custom_providers.dart`, `models_config.dart`, `roles_config.dart`, `providers_queue.dart`) — optional `connectTimeoutMs`/`streamIdleTimeoutMs` fields + strict named-error parsing + yaml/JSON round-trip.
- `cli_config.dart` — `_customProvidersYaml` writes the two optional keys back.
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart` — boot seeding next to the `providerTimeoutsOverride` publish + queue resolution, and the tuning boot notice lines.
- Barrel — two append-only export lines per gh-1232.
- No `stall_*` identifiers (lane #1395's taxonomy untouched); no conn_trace/bench files (lane #1392 untouched).

Consumption note: #1395's ladder adopts `resolveRetryBackoff` + `RetryBudgetLedger` when it lands (the card parameterizes those mechanics — this PR is the tuning/contract layer it tunes with); the settings-hub resilience flow can edit the global section as before; per-entry editing there can ride later.

## Test plan evidence
- `dart test test/providers` — 660 pass (44 new: resolution order, backoff/clamp/edges, budget independence, trace contract, report/recipe, config parsing, boot seeding, loopback wire ITs, adapter-path IT).
- `dart analyze` clean on every touched file; formats limited to my files.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, us…

- **Title**: feat(1398): stall-recovery tuning from the references — per-provider idle timeouts, server-advertised backoff, dual retry budgets
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `feat/1398-stall-recovery-tuning` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 15
- **Additions**: +2367
- **Deletions**: -13
- **Created**: 2026-10-07T23:07:20Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-08T01:06:33Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1398

One sentence: the stall-recovery knobs become per-provider and data-driven — idle/connect timeout, backoff source, and retry budgets resolve per provider entry instead of one global constant, with the tuning recipe computed from measured inter-chunk gaps.

## Delivered vs remaining (AC table)

| AC | status | where |
|---|---|---|
| **AC1** per-provider timeout overrides | ✅ delivered | `providerTuningRegistry` + `resolveProviderTimeouts` (`lib/src/providers/provider_tuning.dart`): entry > `providerTimeouts:` global > 180s/300s defaults, per field. Parsed from `customProviders:`, `models.custom:`, roles chain entries, `providersQueue:` entries (strict positive-int ms). IT: `provider_tuning_loopback_test.dart` — a registered `streamIdleTimeoutMs: 1500` entry fires the idle watchdog at ~1.5s on a real loopback silent stream while an unregistered host keeps the default; the adapter-level UT proves `streamOpenAICompletions` inherits it end-to-end. Boot notices print every seeded entry's effective values (sources labeled `provider:<name>`/`global`/`default`). |
| **AC2** server-advertised backoff | ✅ contract delivered | `resolveRetryBackoff`: parseable delta-seconds `Retry-After` wins for that attempt, hard ceiling 60s with a named clamp (`Retry-After: 300` → 60s + the advertised value on the trace); E2 `0` → absent; E3 malformed/HTTP-date → ladder + note. UT fake-clock suite green. |
| **AC3** dual retry budgets | ✅ delivered | `RetryBudgetLedger`: connection cap 4 / stream cap 3, fully independent counters; UT + IT (five connect-class kills exhaust connection only, the subsequent idle-class stall draws the untouched stream budget; E5 terminal story carries both counts). |
| **AC4** trace format contract | ✅ delivered | `formatRetryTraceLine` — `budget=<connection|stream> attempt=<n>/<cap> delay=<ladder:10s|server:12s|clamp:60s>` + clamp/malformed annotations; format-contract UT pins it. |
| **AC5** data-driven tuning report | ✅ report/seam half | `InterChunkGapRecorder` (per-model p50/p95 nearest-rank + watchdog fires) + `renderTuningReport` with the `streamIdleTimeoutMs ≈ 2× p95` recipe line; empty recorder renders nothing (AC5's "when instrumentation data is present"). **Remaining:** the production feeder is #1392's LatencyMeter + the idle-fire sites — the card names them as the sources; this PR lands the report + the seam they feed. |
| **AC6** REG: byte-identical when untuned | ✅ delivered | empty registry short-circuits to the untouched effective getters; the full `test/providers` suite (660 tests incl. the transient-retry, sse-idle, connect-stall, real-client-watchdog REGs), `test/config` + `cli_config_test` (272), `test/model_roles` (233), `test/parity` (32), hosts + agent-loop + bin-wiring suites all green. |

Edge cases: E1 pinned (defaults stay 300s; codex's 5s explicitly NOT adopted), E2/E3 covered above, E4 the table is read per request so a re-seed applies to the NEXT request while in-flight requests keep theirs, E5 covered.

## Territory note (three lanes in provider files)

New files own everything: `lib/src/providers/provider_tuning.dart`, `lib/src/cli/provider_tuning_seed.dart`, and the three test files. Shared-file surface (all additive, no restructuring):
- `provider_common.dart` — **two minimal additive value-read hunks** (the exact allowance this lane was granted): `_sendWatchedOnce` resolves the connect budget via `providerConnectTimeoutForUrl(request.url)`; `createSseIterator`'s default idle value via `_tunedIdleTimeout(response)` (explicit `idleTimeout` params still win — #1392's watchdog wiring and env plumbing untouched; empty registry returns today's exact values).
- Config parsers (`custom_providers.dart`, `models_config.dart`, `roles_config.dart`, `providers_queue.dart`) — optional `connectTimeoutMs`/`streamIdleTimeoutMs` fields + strict named-error parsing + yaml/JSON round-trip.
- `cli_config.dart` — `_customProvidersYaml` writes the two optional keys back.
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart` — boot seeding next to the `providerTimeoutsOverride` publish + queue resolution, and the tuning boot notice lines.
- Barrel — two append-only export lines per gh-1232.
- No `stall_*` identifiers (lane #1395's taxonomy untouched); no conn_trace/bench files (lane #1392 untouched).

Consumption note: #1395's ladder adopts `resolveRetryBackoff` + `RetryBudgetLedger` when it lands (the card parameterizes those mechanics — this PR is the tuning/contract layer it tunes with); the settings-hub resilience flow can edit the global section as before; per-entry editing there can ride later.

## Test plan evidence
- `dart test test/providers` — 660 pass (44 new: resolution order, backoff/clamp/edges, budget independence, trace contract, report/recipe, config parsing, boot seeding, loopback wire ITs, adapter-path IT).
- `dart analyze` clean on every touched file; formats limited to my files.

Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. blocks.text:
# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, us…
Let me read the input files for the PR review.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1400
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1400
- **Title**: feat(1398): stall-recovery tuning from the references — per-provider idle timeouts, server-advertised backoff, dual retry budgets
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `feat/1398-stall-recovery-tuning` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 15
- **Additions**: +2367
- **Deletions**: -13
- **Created**: 2026-10-07T23:07:20Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-08T01:06:33Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1398

One sentence: the stall-recovery knobs become per-provider and data-driven — idle/connect timeout, backoff source, and retry budgets resolve per provider entry instead of one global constant, with the tuning recipe computed from measured inter-chunk gaps.

## Delivered vs remaining (AC table)

| AC | status | where |
|---|---|---|
| **AC1** per-provider timeout overrides | ✅ delivered | `providerTuningRegistry` + `resolveProviderTimeouts` (`lib/src/providers/provider_tuning.dart`): entry > `providerTimeouts:` global > 180s/300s defaults, per field. Parsed from `customProviders:`, `models.custom:`, roles chain entries, `providersQueue:` entries (strict positive-int ms). IT: `provider_tuning_loopback_test.dart` — a registered `streamIdleTimeoutMs: 1500` entry fires the idle watchdog at ~1.5s on a real loopback silent stream while an unregistered host keeps the default; the adapter-level UT proves `streamOpenAICompletions` inherits it end-to-end. Boot notices print every seeded entry's effective values (sources labeled `provider:<name>`/`global`/`default`). |
| **AC2** server-advertised backoff | ✅ contract delivered | `resolveRetryBackoff`: parseable delta-seconds `Retry-After` wins for that attempt, hard ceiling 60s with a named clamp (`Retry-After: 300` → 60s + the advertised value on the trace); E2 `0` → absent; E3 malformed/HTTP-date → ladder + note. UT fake-clock suite green. |
| **AC3** dual retry budgets | ✅ delivered | `RetryBudgetLedger`: connection cap 4 / stream cap 3, fully independent counters; UT + IT (five connect-class kills exhaust connection only, the subsequent idle-class stall draws the untouched stream budget; E5 terminal story carries both counts). |
| **AC4** trace format contract | ✅ delivered | `formatRetryTraceLine` — `budget=<connection|stream> attempt=<n>/<cap> delay=<ladder:10s|server:12s|clamp:60s>` + clamp/malformed annotations; format-contract UT pins it. |
| **AC5** data-driven tuning report | ✅ report/seam half | `InterChunkGapRecorder` (per-model p50/p95 nearest-rank + watchdog fires) + `renderTuningReport` with the `streamIdleTimeoutMs ≈ 2× p95` recipe line; empty recorder renders nothing (AC5's "when instrumentation data is present"). **Remaining:** the production feeder is #1392's LatencyMeter + the idle-fire sites — the card names them as the sources; this PR lands the report + the seam they feed. |
| **AC6** REG: byte-identical when untuned | ✅ delivered | empty registry short-circuits to the untouched effective getters; the full `test/providers` suite (660 tests incl. the transient-retry, sse-idle, connect-stall, real-client-watchdog REGs), `test/config` + `cli_config_test` (272), `test/model_roles` (233), `test/parity` (32), hosts + agent-loop + bin-wiring suites all green. |

Edge cases: E1 pinned (defaults stay 300s; codex's 5s explicitly NOT adopted), E2/E3 covered above, E4 the table is read per request so a re-seed applies to the NEXT request while in-flight requests keep theirs, E5 covered.

## Territory note (three lanes in provider files)

New files own everything: `lib/src/providers/provider_tuning.dart`, `lib/src/cli/provider_tuning_seed.dart`, and the three test files. Shared-file surface (all additive, no restructuring):
- `provider_common.dart` — **two minimal additive value-read hunks** (the exact allowance this lane was granted): `_sendWatchedOnce` resolves the connect budget via `providerConnectTimeoutForUrl(request.url)`; `createSseIterator`'s default idle value via `_tunedIdleTimeout(response)` (explicit `idleTimeout` params still win — #1392's watchdog wiring and env plumbing untouched; empty registry returns today's exact values).
- Config parsers (`custom_providers.dart`, `models_config.dart`, `roles_config.dart`, `providers_queue.dart`) — optional `connectTimeoutMs`/`streamIdleTimeoutMs` fields + strict named-error parsing + yaml/JSON round-trip.
- `cli_config.dart` — `_customProvidersYaml` writes the two optional keys back.
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart` — boot seeding next to the `providerTimeoutsOverride` publish + queue resolution, and the tuning boot notice lines.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, us…
