Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. # AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, us…

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1400
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1400
- **Title**: feat(1398): stall-recovery tuning from the references — per-provider idle timeouts, server-advertised backoff, dual retry budgets
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `feat/1398-stall-recovery-tuning` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 15
- **Additions**: +2367
- **Deletions**: -13
- **Created**: 2026-10-07T23:07:20Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-08T01:06:33Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1398

One sentence: the stall-recovery knobs become per-provider and data-driven — idle/connect timeout, backoff source, and retry budgets resolve per provider entry instead of one global constant, with the tuning recipe computed from measured inter-chunk gaps.

## Delivered vs remaining (AC table)

| AC | status | where |
|---|---|---|
| **AC1** per-provider timeout overrides | ✅ delivered | `providerTuningRegistry` + `resolveProviderTimeouts` (`lib/src/providers/provider_tuning.dart`): entry > `providerTimeouts:` global > 180s/300s defaults, per field. Parsed from `customProviders:`, `models.custom:`, roles chain entries, `providersQueue:` entries (strict positive-int ms). IT: `provider_tuning_loopback_test.dart` — a registered `streamIdleTimeoutMs: 1500` entry fires the idle watchdog at ~1.5s on a real loopback silent stream while an unregistered host keeps the default; the adapter-level UT proves `streamOpenAICompletions` inherits it end-to-end. Boot notices print every seeded entry's effective values (sources labeled `provider:<name>`/`global`/`default`). |
| **AC2** server-advertised backoff | ✅ contract delivered | `resolveRetryBackoff`: parseable delta-seconds `Retry-After` wins for that attempt, hard ceiling 60s with a named clamp (`Retry-After: 300` → 60s + the advertised value on the trace); E2 `0` → absent; E3 malformed/HTTP-date → ladder + note. UT fake-clock suite green. |
| **AC3** dual retry budgets | ✅ delivered | `RetryBudgetLedger`: connection cap 4 / stream cap 3, fully independent counters; UT + IT (five connect-class kills exhaust connection only, the subsequent idle-class stall draws the untouched stream budget; E5 terminal story carries both counts). |
| **AC4** trace format contract | ✅ delivered | `formatRetryTraceLine` — `budget=<connection|stream> attempt=<n>/<cap> delay=<ladder:10s|server:12s|clamp:60s>` + clamp/malformed annotations; format-contract UT pins it. |
| **AC5** data-driven tuning report | ✅ report/seam half | `InterChunkGapRecorder` (per-model p50/p95 nearest-rank + watchdog fires) + `renderTuningReport` with the `streamIdleTimeoutMs ≈ 2× p95` recipe line; empty recorder renders nothing (AC5's "when instrumentation data is present"). **Remaining:** the production feeder is #1392's LatencyMeter + the idle-fire sites — the card names them as the sources; this PR lands the report + the seam they feed. |
| **AC6** REG: byte-identical when untuned | ✅ delivered | empty registry short-circuits to the untouched effective getters; the full `test/providers` suite (660 tests incl. the transient-retry, sse-idle, connect-stall, real-client-watchdog REGs), `test/config` + `cli_config_test` (272), `test/model_roles` (233), `test/parity` (32), hosts + agent-loop + bin-wiring suites all green. |

Edge cases: E1 pinned (defaults stay 300s; codex's 5s explicitly NOT adopted), E2/E3 covered above, E4 the table is read per request so a re-seed applies to the NEXT request while in-flight requests keep theirs, E5 covered.

## Territory note (three lanes in provider files)

New files own everything: `lib/src/providers/provider_tuning.dart`, `lib/src/cli/provider_tuning_seed.dart`, and the three test files. Shared-file surface (all additive, no restructuring):
- `provider_common.dart` — **two minimal additive value-read hunks** (the exact allowance this lane was granted): `_sendWatchedOnce` resolves the connect budget via `providerConnectTimeoutForUrl(request.url)`; `createSseIterator`'s default idle value via `_tunedIdleTimeout(response)` (explicit `idleTimeout` params still win — #1392's watchdog wiring and env plumbing untouched; empty registry returns today's exact values).
- Config parsers (`custom_providers.dart`, `models_config.dart`, `roles_config.dart`, `providers_queue.dart`) — optional `connectTimeoutMs`/`streamIdleTimeoutMs` fields + strict named-error parsing + yaml/JSON round-trip.
- `cli_config.dart` — `_customProvidersYaml` writes the two optional keys back.
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart` — boot seeding next to the `providerTimeoutsOverride` publish + queue resolution, and the tuning boot notice lines.
- Barrel — two append-only export lines per gh-1232.
- No `stall_*` identifiers (lane #1395's taxonomy untouched); no conn_trace/bench files (lane #1392 untouched).

Consumption note: #1395's ladder adopts `resolveRetryBackoff` + `RetryBudgetLedger` when it lands (the card parameterizes those mechanics — this PR is the tuning/contract layer it tunes with); the settings-hub resilience flow can edit the global section as before; per-entry editing there can ride later.

## Test plan evidence
- `dart test test/providers` — 660 pass (44 new: resolution order, backoff/clamp/edges, budget independence, trace contract, report/recipe, config parsing, boot seeding, loopback wire ITs, adapter-path IT).
- `dart analyze` clean on every touched file; formats limited to my files.

### Thread 9

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-07):
## Automated Code Review — REQUEST_CHANGES

**Summary**: One blocking bug: `providerTuningBootNotices()` is captured *before* queue seeding runs in `bin/fah_runapp.dart`, so queue-carried tuning entries — the lane that replaces main-model resolution — never print their boot notice, contradicting AC1's "every seeded entry" promise. Outside the diff: the `/provider` edit wizard (`_recordSetupEntry` in `provider_commands.dart`) rebuilds entries preserving only `authMethod`, so hand-configured `connectTimeoutMs`/`streamIdleTimeoutMs` are silently dropped when an entry is edited via the wizard — the new config surface needs preserving there like `authMethod`. The tuning/backoff/budget/report contracts are deliberately unwired (territory note), but note the codebase now has two ladder step functions (`providerConnectRetryBackoff * (1 << attempt)` in `provider_common.dart` vs `5 << n` here) and the `retryBackoffLadderStep` doc references `stallBackoffCeiling`, which does not exist yet — a drift risk until #1395 adopts these.

**Key Issues**:
- 🚨 `bin/fah_runapp.dart:247` — queue tuning entries get no boot notice (captured before queue seeding)
- ⚠️ Seeder never resets the table; the documented E4 "config reload re-runs the seeder" is not wired (removed entries would persist forever)
- ⚠️ `forUrl` first-match-wins: overlapping baseUrls resolve by insertion order — a queue entry's own tuning can be silently shadowed by an earlier-registered same-baseUrl entry
- ⚠️ `RetryBudgetLedger.terminalStory()` always says "retry budgets exhausted", even for partial spend (1/4, 0/3) — and a test pins that wording
- 💡 No upper bound in `parseProviderTimeoutMs`; unbounded `InterChunkGapRecorder` growth; `[REDACTED:Sensitive Value]` artifact as the fake key in `provider_tuning_test.dart:451`

**Next Steps**:
1. Build/print the tuning notices after queue resolution (3-line move) + pin with a queue-lane notice test
2. Fix the wizard edit path to carry `connectTimeout`/`streamIdleTimeout` (and `authHeader`) from `existingEntry`
3. Resolve `forUrl` precedence (longest-prefix or last-registration-wins) and reword `terminalStory()` before #1395 pins the format
4. Correct the E4 doc to the actual boot-scoped semantics (or wire the reload)

---

### Thread 10

**vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit** (2026-10-08):
Review r2 addressed in e68b6750e (all 7 threads replied + resolved).

**Blocking** — boot notices now captured AFTER the queue seeding pass (bin/fah_runapp.dart), so queue-carried tuning entries print like every other lane; pinned by a queue-lane notice test + a source-order pin test.

**Important** — (2) the /provider edit wizard carries authMethod/authHeader/connectTimeout/streamIdleTimeout from the existing entry via `mergeEditedCustomProviderEntry`; (3) `forUrl` is longest-base-path-wins, equal-base last-registration-wins — the queue pass can no longer be shadowed by an earlier same-baseUrl entry; (4) `terminalStory()` says "exhausted" only of budgets that actually are (partial spend reads "retry budgets spent (...)"), tests re-pinned to the honest contract; (5) seeder docs corrected to the boot-scoped lifecycle AND `seedProviderTuning(reset: true)` added so a host reload drops removed entries.

**Suggestions** — `parseProviderTimeoutMs` rejects > 1 h (named ConfigException, boundary pinned); `InterChunkGapRecorder` caps per-model samples at 2048 (drop-oldest recent window, pinned); the REDACTED-artifact thread was stale — this PR's tests use `'test-key'`; the marker literals are pre-existing repo convention in files outside this lane.

**Coordination note (#1395)** — the ladder drift risk: `retryBackoffLadderStep`'s doc now references `retryBackoffCeiling` — this module's OWN constant (60 s), defined and used here; the earlier wording named a not-yet-existing `stallBackoffCeiling` symbol, fixed. # AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, us…

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1400
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1400
- **Title**: feat(1398): stall-recovery tuning from the references — per-provider idle timeouts, server-advertised backoff, dual retry budgets
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `feat/1398-stall-recovery-tuning` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 15
- **Additions**: +2367
- **Deletions**: -13
- **Created**: 2026-10-07T23:07:20Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-08T01:06:33Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1398

One sentence: the stall-recovery knobs become per-provider and data-driven — idle/connect timeout, backoff source, and retry budgets resolve per provider entry instead of one global constant, with the tuning recipe computed from measured inter-chunk gaps.

## Delivered vs remaining (AC table)

| AC | status | where |
|---|---|---|
| **AC1** per-provider timeout overrides | ✅ delivered | `providerTuningRegistry` + `resolveProviderTimeouts` (`lib/src/providers/provider_tuning.dart`): entry > `providerTimeouts:` global > 180s/300s defaults, per field. Parsed from `customProviders:`, `models.custom:`, roles chain entries, `providersQueue:` entries (strict positive-int ms). IT: `provider_tuning_loopback_test.dart` — a registered `streamIdleTimeoutMs: 1500` entry fires the idle watchdog at ~1.5s on a real loopback silent stream while an unregistered host keeps the default; the adapter-level UT proves `streamOpenAICompletions` inherits it end-to-end. Boot notices print every seeded entry's effective values (sources labeled `provider:<name>`/`global`/`default`). |
| **AC2** server-advertised backoff | ✅ contract delivered | `resolveRetryBackoff`: parseable delta-seconds `Retry-After` wins for that attempt, hard ceiling 60s with a named clamp (`Retry-After: 300` → 60s + the advertised value on the trace); E2 `0` → absent; E3 malformed/HTTP-date → ladder + note. UT fake-clock suite green. |
| **AC3** dual retry budgets | ✅ delivered | `RetryBudgetLedger`: connection cap 4 / stream cap 3, fully independent counters; UT + IT (five connect-class kills exhaust connection only, the subsequent idle-class stall draws the untouched stream budget; E5 terminal story carries both counts). |
| **AC4** trace format contract | ✅ delivered | `formatRetryTraceLine` — `budget=<connection|stream> attempt=<n>/<cap> delay=<ladder:10s|server:12s|clamp:60s>` + clamp/malformed annotations; format-contract UT pins it. |
| **AC5** data-driven tuning report | ✅ report/seam half | `InterChunkGapRecorder` (per-model p50/p95 nearest-rank + watchdog fires) + `renderTuningReport` with the `streamIdleTimeoutMs ≈ 2× p95` recipe line; empty recorder renders nothing (AC5's "when instrumentation data is present"). **Remaining:** the production feeder is #1392's LatencyMeter + the idle-fire sites — the card names them as the sources; this PR lands the report + the seam they feed. |
| **AC6** REG: byte-identical when untuned | ✅ delivered | empty registry short-circuits to the untouched effective getters; the full `test/providers` suite (660 tests incl. the transient-retry, sse-idle, connect-stall, real-client-watchdog REGs), `test/config` + `cli_config_test` (272), `test/model_roles` (233), `test/parity` (32), hosts + agent-loop + bin-wiring suites all green. |

Edge cases: E1 pinned (defaults stay 300s; codex's 5s explicitly NOT adopted), E2/E3 covered above, E4 the table is read per request so a re-seed applies to the NEXT request while in-flight requests keep theirs, E5 covered.

## Territory note (three lanes in provider files)

New files own everything: `lib/src/providers/provider_tuning.dart`, `lib/src/cli/provider_tuning_seed.dart`, and the three test files. Shared-file surface (all additive, no restructuring):
- `provider_common.dart` — **two minimal additive value-read hunks** (the exact allowance this lane was granted): `_sendWatchedOnce` resolves the connect budget via `providerConnectTimeoutForUrl(request.url)`; `createSseIterator`'s default idle value via `_tunedIdleTimeout(response)` (explicit `idleTimeout` params still win — #1392's watchdog wiring and env plumbing untouched; empty registry returns today's exact values).
- Config parsers (`custom_providers.dart`, `models_config.dart`, `roles_config.dart`, `providers_queue.dart`) — optional `connectTimeoutMs`/`streamIdleTimeoutMs` fields + strict named-error parsing + yaml/JSON round-trip.
- `cli_config.dart` — `_customProvidersYaml` writes the two optional keys back.
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart` — boot seeding next to the `providerTimeoutsOverride` publish + queue resolution, and the tuning boot notice lines.
- Barrel — two append-only export lines per gh-1232.
- No `stall_*` identifiers (lane #1395's taxonomy untouched); no conn_trace/bench files (lane #1392 untouched).

Consumption note: #1395's ladder adopts `resolveRetryBackoff` + `RetryBudgetLedger` when it lands (the card parameterizes those mechanics — this PR is the tuning/contract layer it tunes with); the settings-hub resilience flow can edit the global section as before; per-entry editing there can ride later.

## Test plan evidence
- `dart test test/providers` — 660 pass (44 new: resolution order, backoff/clamp/edges, budget independence, trace contract, report/recipe, config parsing, boot seeding, loopback wire ITs, adapter-path IT).
- `dart analyze` clean on every touched file; formats limited to my files.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, us…

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1400
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1400
- **Title**: feat(1398): stall-recovery tuning from the references — per-provider idle timeouts, server-advertised backoff, dual retry budgets
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `feat/1398-stall-recovery-tuning` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 15
- **Additions**: +2367
- **Deletions**: -13
- **Created**: 2026-10-07T23:07:20Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-08T01:06:33Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1398

One sentence: the stall-recovery knobs become per-provider and data-driven — idle/connect timeout, backoff source, and retry budgets resolve per provider entry instead of one global constant, with the tuning recipe computed from measured inter-chunk gaps.

## Delivered vs remaining (AC table)

| AC | status | where |
|---|---|---|
| **AC1** per-provider timeout overrides | ✅ delivered | `providerTuningRegistry` + `resolveProviderTimeouts` (`lib/src/providers/provider_tuning.dart`): entry > `providerTimeouts:` global > 180s/300s defaults, per field. Parsed from `customProviders:`, `models.custom:`, roles chain entries, `providersQueue:` entries (strict positive-int ms). IT: `provider_tuning_loopback_test.dart` — a registered `streamIdleTimeoutMs: 1500` entry fires the idle watchdog at ~1.5s on a real loopback silent stream while an unregistered host keeps the default; the adapter-level UT proves `streamOpenAICompletions` inherits it end-to-end. Boot notices print every seeded entry's effective values (sources labeled `provider:<name>`/`global`/`default`). |
| **AC2** server-advertised backoff | ✅ contract delivered | `resolveRetryBackoff`: parseable delta-seconds `Retry-After` wins for that attempt, hard ceiling 60s with a named clamp (`Retry-After: 300` → 60s + the advertised value on the trace); E2 `0` → absent; E3 malformed/HTTP-date → ladder + note. UT fake-clock suite green. |
| **AC3** dual retry budgets | ✅ delivered | `RetryBudgetLedger`: connection cap 4 / stream cap 3, fully independent counters; UT + IT (five connect-class kills exhaust connection only, the subsequent idle-class stall draws the untouched stream budget; E5 terminal story carries both counts). |
| **AC4** trace format contract | ✅ delivered | `formatRetryTraceLine` — `budget=<connection|stream> attempt=<n>/<cap> delay=<ladder:10s|server:12s|clamp:60s>` + clamp/malformed annotations; format-contract UT pins it. |
| **AC5** data-driven tuning report | ✅ report/seam half | `InterChunkGapRecorder` (per-model p50/p95 nearest-rank + watchdog fires) + `renderTuningReport` with the `streamIdleTimeoutMs ≈ 2× p95` recipe line; empty recorder renders nothing (AC5's "when instrumentation data is present"). **Remaining:** the production feeder is #1392's LatencyMeter + the idle-fire sites — the card names them as the sources; this PR lands the report + the seam they feed. |
| **AC6** REG: byte-identical when untuned | ✅ delivered | empty registry short-circuits to the untouched effective getters; the full `test/providers` suite (660 tests incl. the transient-retry, sse-idle, connect-stall, real-client-watchdog REGs), `test/config` + `cli_config_test` (272), `test/model_roles` (233), `test/parity` (32), hosts + agent-loop + bin-wiring suites all green. |

Edge cases: E1 pinned (defaults stay 300s; codex's 5s explicitly NOT adopted), E2/E3 covered above, E4 the table is read per request so a re-seed applies to the NEXT request while in-flight requests keep theirs, E5 covered.

## Territory note (three lanes in provider files)

New files own everything: `lib/src/providers/provider_tuning.dart`, `lib/src/cli/provider_tuning_seed.dart`, and the three test files. Shared-file surface (all additive, no restructuring):
- `provider_common.dart` — **two minimal additive value-read hunks** (the exact allowance this lane was granted): `_sendWatchedOnce` resolves the connect budget via `providerConnectTimeoutForUrl(request.url)`; `createSseIterator`'s default idle value via `_tunedIdleTimeout(response)` (explicit `idleTimeout` params still win — #1392's watchdog wiring and env plumbing untouched; empty registry returns today's exact values).
- Config parsers (`custom_providers.dart`, `models_config.dart`, `roles_config.dart`, `providers_queue.dart`) — optional `connectTimeoutMs`/`streamIdleTimeoutMs` fields + strict named-error parsing + yaml/JSON round-trip.
- `cli_config.dart` — `_customProvidersYaml` writes the two optional keys back.
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart` — boot seeding next to the `providerTimeoutsOverride` publish + queue resolution, and the tuning boot notice lines.
- Barrel — two append-only export lines per gh-1232.
- No `stall_*` identifiers (lane #1395's taxonomy untouched); no conn_trace/bench files (lane #1392 untouched).

Consumption note: #1395's ladder adopts `resolveRetryBackoff` + `RetryBudgetLedger` when it lands (the card parameterizes those mechanics — this PR is the tuning/contract layer it tunes with); the settings-hub resilience flow can edit the global section as before; per-entry editing there can ride later.

## Test plan evidence
- `dart test test/providers` — 660 pass (44 new: resolution order, backoff/clamp/edges, budget independence, trace contract, report/recipe, config parsing, boot seeding, loopback wire ITs, adapter-path IT).
- `dart analyze` clean on every touched file; formats limited to my files.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1400
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1400
- **Title**: feat(1398): stall-recovery tuning from the references — per-provider idle timeouts, server-advertised backoff, dual retry budgets
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `feat/1398-stall-recovery-tuning` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 15
- **Additions**: +2367
- **Deletions**: -13
- **Created**: 2026-10-07T23:07:20Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-08T01:06:33Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1398

One sentence: the stall-recovery knobs become per-provider and data-driven — idle/connect timeout, backoff source, and retry budgets resolve per provider entry instead of one global constant, with the tuning recipe computed from measured inter-chunk gaps.

## Delivered vs remaining (AC table)

| AC | status | where |
|---|---|---|
| **AC1** per-provider timeout overrides | ✅ delivered | `providerTuningRegistry` + `resolveProviderTimeouts` (`lib/src/providers/provider_tuning.dart`): entry > `providerTimeouts:` global > 180s/300s defaults, per field. Parsed from `customProviders:`, `models.custom:`, roles chain entries, `providersQueue:` entries (strict positive-int ms). IT: `provider_tuning_loopback_test.dart` — a registered `streamIdleTimeoutMs: 1500` entry fires the idle watchdog at ~1.5s on a real loopback silent stream while an unregistered host keeps the default; the adapter-level UT proves `streamOpenAICompletions` inherits it end-to-end. Boot notices print every seeded entry's effective values (sources labeled `provider:<name>`/`global`/`default`). |
| **AC2** server-advertised backoff | ✅ contract delivered | `resolveRetryBackoff`: parseable delta-seconds `Retry-After` wins for that attempt, hard ceiling 60s with a named clamp (`Retry-After: 300` → 60s + the advertised value on the trace); E2 `0` → absent; E3 malformed/HTTP-date → ladder + note. UT fake-clock suite green. |
| **AC3** dual retry budgets | ✅ delivered | `RetryBudgetLedger`: connection cap 4 / stream cap 3, fully independent counters; UT + IT (five connect-class kills exhaust connection only, the subsequent idle-class stall draws the untouched stream budget; E5 terminal story carries both counts). |
| **AC4** trace format contract | ✅ delivered | `formatRetryTraceLine` — `budget=<connection|stream> attempt=<n>/<cap> delay=<ladder:10s|server:12s|clamp:60s>` + clamp/malformed annotations; format-contract UT pins it. |
| **AC5** data-driven tuning report | ✅ report/seam half | `InterChunkGapRecorder` (per-model p50/p95 nearest-rank + watchdog fires) + `renderTuningReport` with the `streamIdleTimeoutMs ≈ 2× p95` recipe line; empty recorder renders nothing (AC5's "when instrumentation data is present"). **Remaining:** the production feeder is #1392's LatencyMeter + the idle-fire sites — the card names them as the sources; this PR lands the report + the seam they feed. |
| **AC6** REG: byte-identical when untuned | ✅ delivered | empty registry short-circuits to the untouched effective getters; the full `test/providers` suite (660 tests incl. the transient-retry, sse-idle, connect-stall, real-client-watchdog REGs), `test/config` + `cli_config_test` (272), `test/model_roles` (233), `test/parity` (32), hosts + agent-loop + bin-wiring suites all green. |

Edge cases: E1 pinned (defaults stay 300s; codex's 5s explicitly NOT adopted), E2/E3 covered above, E4 the table is read per request so a re-seed applies to the NEXT request while in-flight requests keep theirs, E5 covered.

## Territory note (three lanes in provider files)

New files own everything: `lib/src/providers/provider_tuning.dart`, `lib/src/cli/provider_tuning_seed.dart`, and the three test files. Shared-file surface (all additive, no restructuring):
- `provider_common.dart` — **two minimal additive value-read hunks** (the exact allowance this lane was granted): `_sendWatchedOnce` resolves the connect budget via `providerConnectTimeoutForUrl(request.url)`; `createSseIterator`'s default idle value via `_tunedIdleTimeout(response)` (explicit `idleTimeout` params still win — #1392's watchdog wiring and env plumbing untouched; empty registry returns today's exact values).
- Config parsers (`custom_providers.dart`, `models_config.dart`, `roles_config.dart`, `providers_queue.dart`) — optional `connectTimeoutMs`/`streamIdleTimeoutMs` fields + strict named-error parsing + yaml/JSON round-trip.
- `cli_config.dart` — `_customProvidersYaml` writes the two optional keys back.
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart` — boot seeding next to the `providerTimeoutsOverride` publish + queue resolution, and the tuning boot notice lines.
- Barrel — two append-only export lines per gh-1232.
- No `stall_*` identifiers (lane #1395's taxonomy untouched); no conn_trace/bench files (lane #1392 untouched).

Consumption note: #1395's ladder adopts `resolveRetryBackoff` + `RetryBudgetLedger` when it lands (the card parameterizes those mechanics — this PR is the tuning/contract layer it tunes with); the settings-hub resilience flow can edit the global section as before; per-entry editing there can ride later.

## Test plan evidence
- `dart test test/providers` — 660 pass (44 new: resolution order, backoff/clamp/edges, budget independence, trace contract, report/recipe, config parsing, boot seeding, loopback wire ITs, adapter-path IT).
- `dart analyze` clean on every touched file; formats limited to my files.

# pr-1400: feat(1398): stall-recovery tuning from the references — per-provider idle timeouts, server-advertised backoff, dual retry budgets

## Description

Fixes #1398

One sentence: the stall-recovery knobs become per-provider and data-driven — idle/connect timeout, backoff source, and retry budgets resolve per provider entry instead of one global constant, with the tuning recipe computed from measured inter-chunk gaps.

## Delivered vs remaining (AC table)

| AC | status | where |
|---|---|---|
| **AC1** per-provider timeout overrides | ✅ delivered | `providerTuningRegistry` + `resolveProviderTimeouts` (`lib/src/providers/provider_tuning.dart`): entry > `providerTimeouts:` global > 180s/300s defaults, per field. Parsed from `customProviders:`, `models.custom:`, roles chain entries, `providersQueue:` entries (strict positive-int ms). IT: `provider_tuning_loopback_test.dart` — a registered `streamIdleTimeoutMs: 1500` entry fires the idle watchdog at ~1.5s on a real loopback silent stream while an unregistered host keeps the default; the adapter-level UT proves `streamOpenAICompletions` inherits it end-to-end. Boot notices print every seeded entry's effective values (sources labeled `provider:<name>`/`global`/`default`). |
| **AC2** server-advertised backoff | ✅ contract delivered | `resolveRetryBackoff`: parseable delta-seconds `Retry-After` wins for that attempt, hard ceiling 60s with a named clamp (`Retry-After: 300` → 60s + the advertised value on the trace); E2 `0` → absent; E3 malformed/HTTP-date → ladder + note. UT fake-clock suite green. |
| **AC3** dual retry budgets | ✅ delivered | `RetryBudgetLedger`: connection cap 4 / stream cap 3, fully independent counters; UT + IT (five connect-class kills exhaust connection only, the subsequent idle-class stall draws the untouched stream budget; E5 terminal story carries both counts). |
| **AC4** trace format contract | ✅ delivered | `formatRetryTraceLine` — `budget=<connection|stream> attempt=<n>/<cap> delay=<ladder:10s|server:12s|clamp:60s>` + clamp/malformed annotations; format-contract UT pins it. |
| **AC5** data-driven tuning report | ✅ report/seam half | `InterChunkGapRecorder` (per-model p50/p95 nearest-rank + watchdog fires) + `renderTuningReport` with the `streamIdleTimeoutMs ≈ 2× p95` recipe line; empty recorder renders nothing (AC5's "when instrumentation data is present"). **Remaining:** the production feeder is #1392's LatencyMeter + the idle-fire sites — the card names them as the sources; this PR lands the report + the seam they feed. |
| **AC6** REG: byte-identical when untuned | ✅ delivered | empty registry short-circuits to the untouched effective getters; the full `test/providers` suite (660 tests incl. the transient-retry, sse-idle, connect-stall, real-client-watchdog REGs), `test/config` + `cli_config_test` (272), `test/model_roles` (233), `test/parity` (32), hosts + agent-loop + bin-wiring suites all green. |

Edge cases: E1 pinned (defaults stay 300s; codex's 5s explicitly NOT adopted), E2/E3 covered above, E4 the table is read per request so a re-seed applies to the NEXT request while in-flight requests keep theirs, E5 covered.

## Territory note (three lanes in provider files)

New files own everything: `lib/src/providers/provider_tuning.dart`, `lib/src/cli/provider_tuning_seed.dart`, and the three test files. Shared-file surface (all additive, no restructuring):
- `provider_common.dart` — **two minimal additive value-read hunks** (the exact allowance this lane was granted): `_sendWatchedOnce` resolves the connect budget via `providerConnectTimeoutForUrl(request.url)`; `createSseIterator`'s default idle value via `_tunedIdleTimeout(response)` (explicit `idleTimeout` params still win — #1392's watchdog wiring and env plumbing untouched; empty registry returns today's exact values).
- Config parsers (`custom_providers.dart`, `models_config.dart`, `roles_config.dart`, `providers_queue.dart`) — optional `connectTimeoutMs`/`streamIdleTimeoutMs` fields + strict named-error parsing + yaml/JSON round-trip.
- `cli_config.dart` — `_customProvidersYaml` writes the two optional keys back.
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart` — boot seeding next to the `providerTimeoutsOverride` publish + queue resolution, and the tuning boot notice lines.
- Barrel — two append-only export lines per gh-1232.
- No `stall_*` identifiers (lane #1395's taxonomy untouched); no conn_trace/bench files (lane #1392 untouched).

Consumption note: #1395's ladder adopts `resolveRetryBackoff` + `RetryBudgetLedger` when it lands (the card parameterizes those mechanics — this PR is the tuning/contract layer it tunes with); the settings-hub resilience flow can edit the global section as before; per-entry editing there can ride later.

Found a real gap: `ProviderQueueEntry.resolvedRef` (the `{"ref": name}` queue form) resolves `model`, `baseUrl`, `apiKeyEnv`, `contextWindow`, `maxTokens` from the referenced customProviders entry — but does NOT resolve `connectTimeout`/`streamIdleTimeout` from the referenced entry, and `resolvedRef` has no parameters to receive them either (the `resolveRef` callback signature returns `({String kind, String? baseUrl, String model, String? keyName})` — it doesn't even fetch tuning fields).

Impact: a queue entry `{"ref": my-glm-provider}` where `my-glm-provider` (in customProviders:) declares `streamIdleTimeoutMs: 1500` — the queue entry is seeded via `seedProviderTuning(queueEntries:)` with `connect: null, streamIdle: null` → `ProviderTuningEntry.isEmpty` → NOT registered. So the queue lane's entry is missing from the table.

BUT — the customProviders lane also registered `my-glm-provider` with its tuning (baseUrl same as the materialized ref). So URL lookups still resolve the customProvider's entry → tuning applies. So functionally the watchdog tuning is NOT lost (the seed doc's claim "URL-keyed lookup finds the entry" is exactly this).

Is there any case where the loss matters? If the queue ref's materialized baseUrl DIFFERS from the referenced customProvider's baseUrl (inline `provider_config.baseUrl` override on the ref entry) AND the tuning was on the referenced provider → tuning lost for the overridden URL. Edge of an edge. Also: the boot notice for the customProviders entry prints regardless.

More subtle: `providerTuningBootNotices()` prints entries in the table. The ref'd queue entry itself never appears as `queue:...` — fine, the customProviders line covers it.

So: functional impact is negligible (tuning follows the baseUrl via the config lane), but there IS an inconsistency: a ref+inline-override queue entry pointing at a different baseUrl silently loses the referenced provider's tuning. Given the territory, I'd rate this a SUGGESTION (or borderline IMPORTANT). The wiring to fix it would need `resolveRef` to return tuning fields — a slightly bigger surface. Since the practical case (no baseUrl override on refs) works via the URL-keyed lookup, and the PR doc explicitly documents ref behavior ("Queue `ref` entries need no special handling — they materialize the referenced custom provider's `baseUrl`, so the URL-keyed lookup finds the entry"), the doc is honest for the common case but incomplete for the ref+baseUrl-override case. All correct. Now let me do the exhaustive second pass on the remaining dimensions while gates run:

**Security**: No secrets in the new code — tuning values are durations; boot notices print name+baseUrl+durations (baseUrl was already printed elsewhere; the model line prints provider). `parseProviderTimeoutMs` error messages include the raw value — could echo a config value, but that's standard for config errors. No injection surface. `Retry-After` rawHeader quoted into trace lines — a malicious server could inject arbitrary text into the trace (`retry-after malformed ("<server-controlled>")`). Where do trace lines render? They're part of the AC4 contract for #1395 to consume — logs/session records. A malicious/compromised provider could put a huge or control-char-laden string in Retry-After and it would land in a log line. Log injection is a classic concern but the trace isn't wired yet (#1395). The value is bounded by header size limits (typically 8KB). Low risk — could mention as part of a suggestion? The redaction layer handles secrets; a server-controlled header echoed into logs is standard practice (user agents echo URLs etc.). I'll skip or fold into the drift note. Actually — one real point: `rawHeader` in `formatRetryTraceLine` is quoted raw; when #1395 wires it, a newline in the header could forge log lines. HTTP header values can't contain raw newlines (rejected by parsers), so fine. Skip.

**Duplication**: `_humanize` lives in provider_tuning.dart — is there an existing duration humanizer in formatters.dart (trajectory formatters)? There's `formatters.dart` in trajectory with duration formatting. Potential duplication — a shared `formatDuration` might exist. Let me check.

**Backward compat**: `CustomProviderEntry.toYaml()` return-type widening `Map<String, String>` → `Map<String, Object?>`. Assignments of the result to `Map<String, String>` would break. No in-repo callers. It's a pub-package (hosted) — external consumers could break. Minor BC note — SUGGESTION. Actually wait, is it necessary? `'connectTimeoutMs': ?connectTimeout?.inMilliseconds` — int? value — so yes the map must hold ints now. The widening is necessary. The severity: source-breaking for external users of the barrel who annotated the result type. Dart semantics: return-type widening is source-compatible at call sites using `var`/`final` without explicit type, and `Map<String, Object?>` accepts all previous reads... but not reassignment into `Map<String, String>` typed variables. Minor; mention as a suggestion/BC note. Hmm — for a published package, MAJOR version discipline may apply, but this repo's CHANGELOG doesn't seem to follow semver strictly for such internal APIs. I'll note it briefly.

**ProviderQueueEntry constructor** — new named params added; `const`? It has a body (kind check) so not const. Fine.

Found a real gap: `ProviderQueueEntry.resolvedRef` (the `{"ref": name}` queue form) resolves `model`, `baseUrl`, `apiKeyEnv`, `contextWindow`, `maxTokens` from the referenced customProviders entry — but does NOT resolve `connectTimeout`/`streamIdleTimeout` from the referenced entry, and `resolvedRef` has no parameters to receive them either (the `resolveRef` callback signature returns `({String kind, String? baseUrl, String model, String? keyName})` — it doesn't even fetch tuning fields).

Impact: a queue entry `{"ref": my-glm-provider}` where `my-glm-provider` (in customProviders:) declares `streamIdleTimeoutMs: 1500` — the queue entry is seeded via `seedProviderTuning(queueEntries:)` with `connect: null, streamIdle: null` → `ProviderTuningEntry.isEmpty` → NOT registered. So the queue lane's entry is missing from the table.

BUT — the customProviders lane also registered `my-glm-provider` with its tuning (baseUrl same as the materialized ref). So URL lookups still resolve the customProvider's entry → tuning applies. So functionally the watchdog tuning is NOT lost (the seed doc's claim "URL-keyed lookup finds the entry" is exactly this).

Is there any case where the loss matters? If the queue ref's materialized baseUrl DIFFERS from the referenced customProvider's baseUrl (inline `provider_config.baseUrl` override on the ref entry) AND the tuning was on the referenced provider → tuning lost for the overridden URL. Edge of an edge. Also: the boot notice for the customProviders entry prints regardless.

More subtle: `providerTuningBootNotices()` prints entries in the table. The ref'd queue entry itself never appears as `queue:...` — fine, the customProviders line covers it.

So: functional impact is negligible (tuning follows the baseUrl via the config lane), but there IS an inconsistency: a ref+inline-override queue entry pointing at a different baseUrl silently loses the referenced provider's tuning. Given the territory, I'd rate this a SUGGESTION (or borderline IMPORTANT). The wiring to fix it would need `resolveRef` to return tuning fields — a slightly bigger surface. Since the practical case (no baseUrl override on refs) works via the URL-keyed lookup, and the PR doc explicitly documents ref behavior ("Queue `ref` entries need no special handling — they materialize the referenced custom provider's `baseUrl`, so the URL-keyed lookup finds the entry"), the doc is honest for the common case but incomplete for the ref+baseUrl-override case. blocks.text:
All correct. Now let me do the exhaustive second pass on the remaining dimensions while gates run:

**Security**: No secrets in the new code — tuning values are durations; boot notices print name+baseUrl+durations (baseUrl was already printed elsewhere; the model line prints provider). `parseProviderTimeoutMs` error messages include the raw value — could echo a config value, but that's standard for config errors. No injection surface. `Retry-After` rawHeader quoted into trace lines — a malicious server could inject arbitrary text into the trace (`retry-after malformed ("<server-controlled>")`). Where do trace lines render? They're part of the AC4 contract for #1395 to consume — logs/session records. A malicious/compromised provider could put a huge or control-char-laden string in Retry-After and it would land in a log line. Log injection is a classic concern but the trace isn't wired yet (#1395). The value is bounded by header size limits (typically 8KB). Low risk — could mention as part of a suggestion? The redaction layer handles secrets; a server-controlled header echoed into logs is standard practice (user agents echo URLs etc.). I'll skip or fold into the drift note. Actually — one real point: `rawHeader` in `formatRetryTraceLine` is quoted raw; when #1395 wires it, a newline in the header could forge log lines. HTTP header values can't contain raw newlines (rejected by parsers), so fine. Skip.

**Duplication**: `_humanize` lives in provider_tuning.dart — is there an existing duration humanizer in formatters.dart (trajectory formatters)? There's `formatters.dart` in trajectory with duration formatting. Potential duplication — a shared `formatDuration` might exist. Let me check.

**Backward compat**: `CustomProviderEntry.toYaml()` return-type widening `Map<String, String>` → `Map<String, Object?>`. Assignments of the result to `Map<String, String>` would break. No in-repo callers. It's a pub-package (hosted) — external consumers could break. Minor BC note — SUGGESTION. Actually wait, is it necessary? `'connectTimeoutMs': ?connectTimeout?.inMilliseconds` — int? value — so yes the map must hold ints now. The widening is necessary. The severity: source-breaking for external users of the barrel who annotated the result type. Dart semantics: return-type widening is source-compatible at call sites using `var`/`final` without explicit type, and `Map<String, Object?>` accepts all previous reads... but not reassignment into `Map<String, String>` typed variables. Minor; mention as a suggestion/BC note. Hmm — for a published package, MAJOR version discipline may apply, but this repo's CHANGELOG doesn't seem to follow semver strictly for such internal APIs. I'll note it briefly.

**ProviderQueueEntry constructor** — new named params added; `const`? It has a body (kind check) so not const. Fine.

Missing test coverage: `_matchesBaseUrl` edge — entry baseUrl with no path (matches any path) IS covered via loopback (baseUrl without path, request /v1/chat). ✔.

**Error paths**: parse errors name field+entry ✔.

**The remaining findings so far:**
1. SUGGESTION: `resolvedRef` (queue `{"ref": ...}` + inline `provider_config`) silently ignores `connectTimeoutMs`/`streamIdleTimeoutMs` — inconsistent with the strict-parse philosophy; currently test-only path (production boot never passes resolveRef), so consistency fix can ride whenever ref resolution gets wired.

SUGGESTION: `providerTuningBootNotices()` resolves values via `forName`, so two same-name entries (e.g. a role chain listing the same `provider/model` twice with different tuning) would print the first entry's values for both lines. Edge case. Actually wait — can a role chain legitimately contain the same ModelRef label twice? `roles: default: [openai/gpt-4o, openai/gpt-4o]`? Unusual. And both would be distinct entries only if their tuning fields differ. Marginal. Also `register` would replace per (name, baseUrl) — same name+same baseUrl+same values → one row. Same name, different baseUrl (different baseUrls for same provider/model in two chains?) → two rows, notices both resolve to the first. OK marginal but real inconsistency with the "print every seeded entry's effective values" promise. Keep as SUGGESTION.

Only within-lane same-name-different-baseUrl: customProviders names are unique (registry enforced?) — let me verify CustomProviderRegistry enforces unique names. `mergeCustomProviderEntries`... `/provider` save replaces by name. Found a real gap: `ProviderQueueEntry.resolvedRef` (the `{"ref": name}` queue form) resolves `model`, `baseUrl`, `apiKeyEnv`, `contextWindow`, `maxTokens` from the referenced customProviders entry — but does NOT resolve `connectTimeout`/`streamIdleTimeout` from the referenced entry, and `resolvedRef` has no parameters to receive them either (the `resolveRef` callback signature returns `({String kind, String? baseUrl, String model, String? keyName})` — it doesn't even fetch tuning fields).

Impact: a queue entry `{"ref": my-glm-provider}` where `my-glm-provider` (in customProviders:) declares `streamIdleTimeoutMs: 1500` — the queue entry is seeded via `seedProviderTuning(queueEntries:)` with `connect: null, streamIdle: null` → `ProviderTuningEntry.isEmpty` → NOT registered. So the queue lane's entry is missing from the table.

BUT — the customProviders lane also registered `my-glm-provider` with its tuning (baseUrl same as the materialized ref). So URL lookups still resolve the customProvider's entry → tuning applies. So functionally the watchdog tuning is NOT lost (the seed doc's claim "URL-keyed lookup finds the entry" is exactly this).

Is there any case where the loss matters? If the queue ref's materialized baseUrl DIFFERS from the referenced customProvider's baseUrl (inline `provider_config.baseUrl` override on the ref entry) AND the tuning was on the referenced provider → tuning lost for the overridden URL. Edge of an edge. Also: the boot notice for the customProviders entry prints regardless.

More subtle: `providerTuningBootNotices()` prints entries in the table. The ref'd queue entry itself never appears as `queue:...` — fine, the customProviders line covers it.

So: functional impact is negligible (tuning follows the baseUrl via the config lane), but there IS an inconsistency: a ref+inline-override queue entry pointing at a different baseUrl silently loses the referenced provider's tuning. Given the territory, I'd rate this a SUGGESTION (or borderline IMPORTANT). The wiring to fix it would need `resolveRef` to return tuning fields — a slightly bigger surface. Since the practical case (no baseUrl override on refs) works via the URL-keyed lookup, and the PR doc explicitly documents ref behavior ("Queue `ref` entries need no special handling — they materialize the referenced custom provider's `baseUrl`, so the URL-keyed lookup finds the entry"), the doc is honest for the common case but incomplete for the ref+baseUrl-override case. I'll file as SUGGESTION with the concrete edge case.

That's inconsistent with the strict-parse philosophy ("a typo must never silently keep the default") — a user setting `provider_config.streamIdleTimeoutMs` on a ref entry gets NOTHING: no override, no error. blocks.text:
Found a real gap: `ProviderQueueEntry.resolvedRef` (the `{"ref": name}` queue form) resolves `model`, `baseUrl`, `apiKeyEnv`, `contextWindow`, `maxTokens` from the referenced customProviders entry — but does NOT resolve `connectTimeout`/`streamIdleTimeout` from the referenced entry, and `resolvedRef` has no parameters to receive them either (the `resolveRef` callback signature returns `({String kind, String? baseUrl, String model, String? keyName})` — it doesn't even fetch tuning fields).

Impact: a queue entry `{"ref": my-glm-provider}` where `my-glm-provider` (in customProviders:) declares `streamIdleTimeoutMs: 1500` — the queue entry is seeded via `seedProviderTuning(queueEntries:)` with `connect: null, streamIdle: null` → `ProviderTuningEntry.isEmpty` → NOT registered. So the queue lane's entry is missing from the table.

BUT — the customProviders lane also registered `my-glm-provider` with its tuning (baseUrl same as the materialized ref). So URL lookups still resolve the customProvider's entry → tuning applies. So functionally the watchdog tuning is NOT lost (the seed doc's claim "URL-keyed lookup finds the entry" is exactly this).

Is there any case where the loss matters? If the queue ref's materialized baseUrl DIFFERS from the referenced customProvider's baseUrl (inline `provider_config.baseUrl` override on the ref entry) AND the tuning was on the referenced provider → tuning lost for the overridden URL. Edge of an edge. Also: the boot notice for the customProviders entry prints regardless.

More subtle: `providerTuningBootNotices()` prints entries in the table. The ref'd queue entry itself never appears as `queue:...` — fine, the customProviders line covers it.

So: functional impact is negligible (tuning follows the baseUrl via the config lane), but there IS an inconsistency: a ref+inline-override queue entry pointing at a different baseUrl silently loses the referenced provider's tuning. Given the territory, I'd rate this a SUGGESTION (or borderline IMPORTANT). The wiring to fix it would need `resolveRef` to return tuning fields — a slightly bigger surface. Since the practical case (no baseUrl override on refs) works via the URL-keyed lookup, and the PR doc explicitly documents ref behavior ("Queue `ref` entries need no special handling — they materialize the referenced custom provider's `baseUrl`, so the URL-keyed lookup finds the entry"), the doc is honest for the common case but incomplete for the ref+baseUrl-override case. I'll file as SUGGESTION with the concrete edge case.

Hmm, wait — actually, let me reconsider. Is `resolvedRef` even in the production boot path? `resolveProviderQueueAtBoot` → parse → entries. Let me check where resolvedRef is called with the resolveRef callback — in startup.dart presumably, resolving against `saved.customProviders`. Let me quickly confirm.

Also — the E4 gap on `resolvedRef`: `overrides` (inline provider_config) is parsed for model/baseUrl/apiKeyEnv/contextWindow/maxTokens — but NOT for connectTimeoutMs/streamIdleTimeoutMs! So a ref entry with inline `provider_config: {streamIdleTimeoutMs: 1500}` override SILENTLY DROPS the tuning key (no parse, no error). That's inconsistent with the strict-parse philosophy ("a typo must never silently keep the default") — a user setting `provider_config.streamIdleTimeoutMs` on a ref entry gets NOTHING: no override, no error. THAT is a real (if small) correctness gap within the PR's own AC1 scope ("Parsed from customProviders:, models.custom:, roles chain entries, providersQueue: entries"). The PR claims queue entries parse these keys — the direct form does; the ref+override form silently ignores them. I'd rate this IMPORTANT — real correctness/consistency gap in the new config surface, silent (violates the card's own strict-parse promise), but not a crash/security/data-loss bug.
