blocks.text:
All correct. Now let me do the exhaustive second pass on the remaining dimensions while gates run:

**Security**: No secrets in the new code — tuning values are durations; boot notices print name+baseUrl+durations (baseUrl was already printed elsewhere; the model line prints provider). `parseProviderTimeoutMs` error messages include the raw value — could echo a config value, but that's standard for config errors. No injection surface. `Retry-After` rawHeader quoted into trace lines — a malicious server could inject arbitrary text into the trace (`retry-after malformed ("<server-controlled>")`). Where do trace lines render? They're part of the AC4 contract for #1395 to consume — logs/session records. A malicious/compromised provider could put a huge or control-char-laden string in Retry-After and it would land in a log line. Log injection is a classic concern but the trace isn't wired yet (#1395). The value is bounded by header size limits (typically 8KB). Low risk — could mention as part of a suggestion? The redaction layer handles secrets; a server-controlled header echoed into logs is standard practice (user agents echo URLs etc.). I'll skip or fold into the drift note. Actually — one real point: `rawHeader` in `formatRetryTraceLine` is quoted raw; when #1395 wires it, a newline in the header could forge log lines. HTTP header values can't contain raw newlines (rejected by parsers), so fine. Skip.

**Duplication**: `_humanize` lives in provider_tuning.dart — is there an existing duration humanizer in formatters.dart (trajectory formatters)? There's `formatters.dart` in trajectory with duration formatting. Potential duplication — a shared `formatDuration` might exist. Let me check.

**Backward compat**: `CustomProviderEntry.toYaml()` return-type widening `Map<String, String>` → `Map<String, Object?>`. Assignments of the result to `Map<String, String>` would break. No in-repo callers. It's a pub-package (hosted) — external consumers could break. Minor BC note — SUGGESTION. Actually wait, is it necessary? `'connectTimeoutMs': ?connectTimeout?.inMilliseconds` — int? value — so yes the map must hold ints now. The widening is necessary. The severity: source-breaking for external users of the barrel who annotated the result type. Dart semantics: return-type widening is source-compatible at call sites using `var`/`final` without explicit type, and `Map<String, Object?>` accepts all previous reads... but not reassignment into `Map<String, String>` typed variables. Minor; mention as a suggestion/BC note. Hmm — for a published package, MAJOR version discipline may apply, but this repo's CHANGELOG doesn't seem to follow semver strictly for such internal APIs. I'll note it briefly.

**ProviderQueueEntry constructor** — new named params added; `const`? It has a body (kind check) so not const. Fine.

**Tests coverage of changed behavior**:
- resolution order ✅, per-field ✅, port/scheme ✅, precedence ✅, name lookup ✅, describe ✅
- backoff ladder ✅ edges ✅
- budgets ✅ + honest story ✅
- trace ✅
- report ✅ bounded ✅
- config parsing all 4 surfaces ✅ round-trip ✅ wizard carry ✅ (via mergeEdited unit test; not a full wizard drive test — but the wizard suite (72) existed and the merge seam is unit-tested; the actual `_recordSetupEntry` wiring is thin glue)
- boot seeding ✅ + queue-lane notice ✅ + source-order pin ✅
- loopback ITs ✅ + adapter-path IT ✅
- reset semantics ✅

Missing test coverage: `_matchesBaseUrl` edge — entry baseUrl with no path (matches any path) IS covered via loopback (baseUrl without path, request /v1/chat). ✔.

**Error paths**: parse errors name field+entry ✔.

**The remaining findings so far:**
1. SUGGESTION: `resolvedRef` (queue `{"ref": ...}` + inline `provider_config`) silently ignores `connectTimeoutMs`/`streamIdleTimeoutMs` — inconsistent with the strict-parse philosophy; currently test-only path (production boot never passes resolveRef), so consistency fix can ride whenever ref resolution gets wired.
2. SUGGESTION: `providerTuningBootNotices()` resolves values via `forName`, so two same-name entries (e.g. a role chain listing the same `provider/model` twice with different tuning) would print the first entry's values for both lines. Edge case. Actually wait — can a role chain legitimately contain the same ModelRef label twice? `roles: default: [openai/gpt-4o, openai/gpt-4o]`? Unusual. And both would be distinct entries only if their tuning fields differ. Marginal. Also `register` would replace per (name, baseUrl) — same name+same baseUrl+same values → one row. Same name, different baseUrl (different baseUrls for same provider/model in two chains?) → two rows, notices both resolve to the first. OK marginal but real inconsistency with the "print every seeded entry's effective values" promise. Keep as SUGGESTION.

Actually, hold on — there's a subtler version: TWO DIFFERENT entries, one named `glm-relay` (customProviders) and another whose label collides... lanes are namespaced, so no. Only within-lane same-name-different-baseUrl: customProviders names are unique (registry enforced?) — let me verify CustomProviderRegistry enforces unique names. `mergeCustomProviderEntries`... `/provider` save replaces by name. Yaml parse: could a hand-edited config declare two entries with the same name? Let me check fromYaml loop — does it dedup/error? If hand-edited yaml can carry duplicate names, then two tuning rows with the same name and different baseUrls are possible and the notice for the second shows the first's values. Let me check quickly.

3. Check `formatters` duplication: look for an existing humanize-duration helper.

4. `toYaml` widening BC note (SUGGESTION).

5. Possibly note the CI status: validation re-ran after 1cf19f60f (thread 13 says re-entering validation). No ci_failures.md input → no red to report. My own gates will confirm.

Let me check items 2 (duplicate names) and 3 (formatter duplication).

BUT — the customProviders lane also registered `my-glm-provider` with its tuning (baseUrl same as the materialized ref). So URL lookups still resolve the customProvider's entry → tuning applies. So functionally the watchdog tuning is NOT lost (the seed doc's claim "URL-keyed lookup finds the entry" is exactly this).

If the queue ref's materialized baseUrl DIFFERS from the referenced customProvider's baseUrl (inline `provider_config.baseUrl` override on the ref entry) AND the tuning was on the referenced provider → tuning lost for the overridden URL. All correct. Now let me do the exhaustive second pass on the remaining dimensions while gates run:

**Security**: No secrets in the new code — tuning values are durations; boot notices print name+baseUrl+durations (baseUrl was already printed elsewhere; the model line prints provider). `parseProviderTimeoutMs` error messages include the raw value — could echo a config value, but that's standard for config errors. No injection surface. `Retry-After` rawHeader quoted into trace lines — a malicious server could inject arbitrary text into the trace (`retry-after malformed ("<server-controlled>")`). Where do trace lines render? They're part of the AC4 contract for #1395 to consume — logs/session records. A malicious/compromised provider could put a huge or control-char-laden string in Retry-After and it would land in a log line. Log injection is a classic concern but the trace isn't wired yet (#1395). The value is bounded by header size limits (typically 8KB). Low risk — could mention as part of a suggestion? The redaction layer handles secrets; a server-controlled header echoed into logs is standard practice (user agents echo URLs etc.). I'll skip or fold into the drift note. Actually — one real point: `rawHeader` in `formatRetryTraceLine` is quoted raw; when #1395 wires it, a newline in the header could forge log lines. HTTP header values can't contain raw newlines (rejected by parsers), so fine. Skip.

**Duplication**: `_humanize` lives in provider_tuning.dart — is there an existing duration humanizer in formatters.dart (trajectory formatters)? There's `formatters.dart` in trajectory with duration formatting. Potential duplication — a shared `formatDuration` might exist. Let me check.

**Backward compat**: `CustomProviderEntry.toYaml()` return-type widening `Map<String, String>` → `Map<String, Object?>`. Assignments of the result to `Map<String, String>` would break. No in-repo callers. It's a pub-package (hosted) — external consumers could break. Minor BC note — SUGGESTION. Actually wait, is it necessary? `'connectTimeoutMs': ?connectTimeout?.inMilliseconds` — int? value — so yes the map must hold ints now. The widening is necessary. The severity: source-breaking for external users of the barrel who annotated the result type. Dart semantics: return-type widening is source-compatible at call sites using `var`/`final` without explicit type, and `Map<String, Object?>` accepts all previous reads... but not reassignment into `Map<String, String>` typed variables. Minor; mention as a suggestion/BC note. Hmm — for a published package, MAJOR version discipline may apply, but this repo's CHANGELOG doesn't seem to follow semver strictly for such internal APIs. I'll note it briefly.

**ProviderQueueEntry constructor** — new named params added; `const`? It has a body (kind check) so not const. Fine.

- resolution order ✅, per-field ✅, port/scheme ✅, precedence ✅, name lookup ✅, describe ✅

Missing test coverage: `_matchesBaseUrl` edge — entry baseUrl with no path (matches any path) IS covered via loopback (baseUrl without path, request /v1/chat). ✔.

**Error paths**: parse errors name field+entry ✔.

**The remaining findings so far:**
1. SUGGESTION: `resolvedRef` (queue `{"ref": ...}` + inline `provider_config`) silently ignores `connectTimeoutMs`/`streamIdleTimeoutMs` — inconsistent with the strict-parse philosophy; currently test-only path (production boot never passes resolveRef), so consistency fix can ride whenever ref resolution gets wired.
2. SUGGESTION: `providerTuningBootNotices()` resolves values via `forName`, so two same-name entries (e.g. a role chain listing the same `provider/model` twice with different tuning) would print the first entry's values for both lines. Edge case. Actually wait — can a role chain legitimately contain the same ModelRef label twice? `roles: default: [openai/gpt-4o, openai/gpt-4o]`? Unusual. And both would be distinct entries only if their tuning fields differ. Marginal. Also `register` would replace per (name, baseUrl) — same name+same baseUrl+same values → one row. Same name, different baseUrl (different baseUrls for same provider/model in two chains?) → two rows, notices both resolve to the first. OK marginal but real inconsistency with the "print every seeded entry's effective values" promise. Keep as SUGGESTION.

Actually, hold on — there's a subtler version: TWO DIFFERENT entries, one named `glm-relay` (customProviders) and another whose label collides... lanes are namespaced, so no. Only within-lane same-name-different-baseUrl: customProviders names are unique (registry enforced?) — let me verify CustomProviderRegistry enforces unique names. `mergeCustomProviderEntries`... `/provider` save replaces by name. Now let me examine the changed areas for issues.

Observations so far:

1. `providerTuningBootNotices()` uses `resolveProviderTimeouts(name: entry.name)` — if two entries share the same `name` (e.g. a customProviders entry named `foo` and a models.custom key `foo` → name `models.custom.foo` so different; but a customProviders entry `foo` and a role ref labeled `provider/model` — role refs use `role:<label>`; queue entries use `queue:<label>`), the names are mostly namespaced. But customProviders names are user-defined and models.custom are prefixed with `models.custom.`, role refs `role:`, queue `queue:`. So cross-lane duplicate name is only possible between two customProviders entries with the same name — but the customProviders registry itself disallows duplicate names (probably). blocks.text:
Found a real gap: `ProviderQueueEntry.resolvedRef` (the `{"ref": name}` queue form) resolves `model`, `baseUrl`, `apiKeyEnv`, `contextWindow`, `maxTokens` from the referenced customProviders entry — but does NOT resolve `connectTimeout`/`streamIdleTimeout` from the referenced entry, and `resolvedRef` has no parameters to receive them either (the `resolveRef` callback signature returns `({String kind, String? baseUrl, String model, String? keyName})` — it doesn't even fetch tuning fields).

Impact: a queue entry `{"ref": my-glm-provider}` where `my-glm-provider` (in customProviders:) declares `streamIdleTimeoutMs: 1500` — the queue entry is seeded via `seedProviderTuning(queueEntries:)` with `connect: null, streamIdle: null` → `ProviderTuningEntry.isEmpty` → NOT registered. So the queue lane's entry is missing from the table.

BUT — the customProviders lane also registered `my-glm-provider` with its tuning (baseUrl same as the materialized ref). So URL lookups still resolve the customProvider's entry → tuning applies. So functionally the watchdog tuning is NOT lost (the seed doc's claim "URL-keyed lookup finds the entry" is exactly this).

Is there any case where the loss matters? If the queue ref's materialized baseUrl DIFFERS from the referenced customProvider's baseUrl (inline `provider_config.baseUrl` override on the ref entry) AND the tuning was on the referenced provider → tuning lost for the overridden URL. Edge of an edge. Also: the boot notice for the customProviders entry prints regardless.

More subtle: `providerTuningBootNotices()` prints entries in the table. The ref'd queue entry itself never appears as `queue:...` — fine, the customProviders line covers it.

So: functional impact is negligible (tuning follows the baseUrl via the config lane), but there IS an inconsistency: a ref+inline-override queue entry pointing at a different baseUrl silently loses the referenced provider's tuning. Given the territory, I'd rate this a SUGGESTION (or borderline IMPORTANT). The wiring to fix it would need `resolveRef` to return tuning fields — a slightly bigger surface. Since the practical case (no baseUrl override on refs) works via the URL-keyed lookup, and the PR doc explicitly documents ref behavior ("Queue `ref` entries need no special handling — they materialize the referenced custom provider's `baseUrl`, so the URL-keyed lookup finds the entry"), the doc is honest for the common case but incomplete for the ref+baseUrl-override case. I'll file as SUGGESTION with the concrete edge case.

Hmm, wait — actually, let me reconsider. Is `resolvedRef` even in the production boot path? `resolveProviderQueueAtBoot` → parse → entries. Let me check where resolvedRef is called with the resolveRef callback — in startup.dart presumably, resolving against `saved.customProviders`. Let me quickly confirm.

Also — the E4 gap on `resolvedRef`: `overrides` (inline provider_config) is parsed for model/baseUrl/apiKeyEnv/contextWindow/maxTokens — but NOT for connectTimeoutMs/streamIdleTimeoutMs! So a ref entry with inline `provider_config: {streamIdleTimeoutMs: 1500}` override SILENTLY DROPS the tuning key (no parse, no error). That's inconsistent with the strict-parse philosophy ("a typo must never silently keep the default") — a user setting `provider_config.streamIdleTimeoutMs` on a ref entry gets NOTHING: no override, no error. THAT is a real (if small) correctness gap within the PR's own AC1 scope ("Parsed from customProviders:, models.custom:, roles chain entries, providersQueue: entries"). The PR claims queue entries parse these keys — the direct form does; the ref+override form silently ignores them. I'd rate this IMPORTANT — real correctness/consistency gap in the new config surface, silent (violates the card's own strict-parse promise), but not a crash/security/data-loss bug.

No injection surface. `Retry-After` rawHeader quoted into trace lines — a malicious server could inject arbitrary text into the trace (`retry-after malformed ("<server-controlled>")`). Where do trace lines render? They're part of the AC4 contract for #1395 to consume — logs/session records. A malicious/compromised provider could put a huge or control-char-laden string in Retry-After and it would land in a log line. Log injection is a classic concern but the trace isn't wired yet (#1395). The value is bounded by header size limits (typically 8KB). Low risk — could mention as part of a suggestion? The redaction layer handles secrets; a server-controlled header echoed into logs is standard practice (user agents echo URLs etc.). I'll skip or fold into the drift note. Actually — one real point: `rawHeader` in `formatRetryTraceLine` is quoted raw; when #1395 wires it, a newline in the header could forge log lines. HTTP header values can't contain raw newlines (rejected by parsers), so fine. Skip.

**Duplication**: `_humanize` lives in provider_tuning.dart — is there an existing duration humanizer in formatters.dart (trajectory formatters)? There's `formatters.dart` in trajectory with duration formatting. Potential duplication — a shared `formatDuration` might exist. Let me check.

No in-repo callers. It's a pub-package (hosted) — external consumers could break. Minor BC note — SUGGESTION. Actually wait, is it necessary? `'connectTimeoutMs': ?connectTimeout?.inMilliseconds` — int? value — so yes the map must hold ints now. The widening is necessary. The severity: source-breaking for external users of the barrel who annotated the result type. Dart semantics: return-type widening is source-compatible at call sites using `var`/`final` without explicit type, and `Map<String, Object?>` accepts all previous reads... but not reassignment into `Map<String, String>` typed variables. Minor; mention as a suggestion/BC note. Hmm — for a published package, MAJOR version discipline may apply, but this repo's CHANGELOG doesn't seem to follow semver strictly for such internal APIs. I'll note it briefly.

Found a real gap: `ProviderQueueEntry.resolvedRef` (the `{"ref": name}` queue form) resolves `model`, `baseUrl`, `apiKeyEnv`, `contextWindow`, `maxTokens` from the referenced customProviders entry — but does NOT resolve `connectTimeout`/`streamIdleTimeout` from the referenced entry, and `resolvedRef` has no parameters to receive them either (the `resolveRef` callback signature returns `({String kind, String? baseUrl, String model, String? keyName})` — it doesn't even fetch tuning fields).

Impact: a queue entry `{"ref": my-glm-provider}` where `my-glm-provider` (in customProviders:) declares `streamIdleTimeoutMs: 1500` — the queue entry is seeded via `seedProviderTuning(queueEntries:)` with `connect: null, streamIdle: null` → `ProviderTuningEntry.isEmpty` → NOT registered. So the queue lane's entry is missing from the table.

BUT — the customProviders lane also registered `my-glm-provider` with its tuning (baseUrl same as the materialized ref). So URL lookups still resolve the customProvider's entry → tuning applies. So functionally the watchdog tuning is NOT lost (the seed doc's claim "URL-keyed lookup finds the entry" is exactly this).

Is there any case where the loss matters? If the queue ref's materialized baseUrl DIFFERS from the referenced customProvider's baseUrl (inline `provider_config.baseUrl` override on the ref entry) AND the tuning was on the referenced provider → tuning lost for the overridden URL. Edge of an edge. Also: the boot notice for the customProviders entry prints regardless.

More subtle: `providerTuningBootNotices()` prints entries in the table. The ref'd queue entry itself never appears as `queue:...` — fine, the customProviders line covers it.

So: functional impact is negligible (tuning follows the baseUrl via the config lane), but there IS an inconsistency: a ref+inline-override queue entry pointing at a different baseUrl silently loses the referenced provider's tuning. Given the territory, I'd rate this a SUGGESTION (or borderline IMPORTANT). The wiring to fix it would need `resolveRef` to return tuning fields — a slightly bigger surface. Since the practical case (no baseUrl override on refs) works via the URL-keyed lookup, and the PR doc explicitly documents ref behavior ("Queue `ref` entries need no special handling — they materialize the referenced custom provider's `baseUrl`, so the URL-keyed lookup finds the entry"), the doc is honest for the common case but incomplete for the ref+baseUrl-override case. blocks.text:
All correct. Now let me do the exhaustive second pass on the remaining dimensions while gates run:

**Security**: No secrets in the new code — tuning values are durations; boot notices print name+baseUrl+durations (baseUrl was already printed elsewhere; the model line prints provider). `parseProviderTimeoutMs` error messages include the raw value — could echo a config value, but that's standard for config errors. No injection surface. `Retry-After` rawHeader quoted into trace lines — a malicious server could inject arbitrary text into the trace (`retry-after malformed ("<server-controlled>")`). Where do trace lines render? They're part of the AC4 contract for #1395 to consume — logs/session records. A malicious/compromised provider could put a huge or control-char-laden string in Retry-After and it would land in a log line. Log injection is a classic concern but the trace isn't wired yet (#1395). The value is bounded by header size limits (typically 8KB). Low risk — could mention as part of a suggestion? The redaction layer handles secrets; a server-controlled header echoed into logs is standard practice (user agents echo URLs etc.). I'll skip or fold into the drift note. Actually — one real point: `rawHeader` in `formatRetryTraceLine` is quoted raw; when #1395 wires it, a newline in the header could forge log lines. HTTP header values can't contain raw newlines (rejected by parsers), so fine. Skip.

**Duplication**: `_humanize` lives in provider_tuning.dart — is there an existing duration humanizer in formatters.dart (trajectory formatters)? There's `formatters.dart` in trajectory with duration formatting. Potential duplication — a shared `formatDuration` might exist. Let me check.

**Backward compat**: `CustomProviderEntry.toYaml()` return-type widening `Map<String, String>` → `Map<String, Object?>`. Assignments of the result to `Map<String, String>` would break. No in-repo callers. It's a pub-package (hosted) — external consumers could break. Minor BC note — SUGGESTION. Actually wait, is it necessary? `'connectTimeoutMs': ?connectTimeout?.inMilliseconds` — int? value — so yes the map must hold ints now. The widening is necessary. The severity: source-breaking for external users of the barrel who annotated the result type. Dart semantics: return-type widening is source-compatible at call sites using `var`/`final` without explicit type, and `Map<String, Object?>` accepts all previous reads... but not reassignment into `Map<String, String>` typed variables. Minor; mention as a suggestion/BC note. Hmm — for a published package, MAJOR version discipline may apply, but this repo's CHANGELOG doesn't seem to follow semver strictly for such internal APIs. I'll note it briefly.

**ProviderQueueEntry constructor** — new named params added; `const`? It has a body (kind check) so not const. Fine.

**Tests coverage of changed behavior**:
- resolution order ✅, per-field ✅, port/scheme ✅, precedence ✅, name lookup ✅, describe ✅
- backoff ladder ✅ edges ✅
- budgets ✅ + honest story ✅

- report ✅ bounded ✅

- boot seeding ✅ + queue-lane notice ✅ + source-order pin ✅
- loopback ITs ✅ + adapter-path IT ✅
- reset semantics ✅

Missing test coverage: `_matchesBaseUrl` edge — entry baseUrl with no path (matches any path) IS covered via loopback (baseUrl without path, request /v1/chat). ✔.

**Error paths**: parse errors name field+entry ✔.

**The remaining findings so far:**
1. SUGGESTION: `resolvedRef` (queue `{"ref": ...}` + inline `provider_config`) silently ignores `connectTimeoutMs`/`streamIdleTimeoutMs` — inconsistent with the strict-parse philosophy; currently test-only path (production boot never passes resolveRef), so consistency fix can ride whenever ref resolution gets wired.
2. SUGGESTION: `providerTuningBootNotices()` resolves values via `forName`, so two same-name entries (e.g. a role chain listing the same `provider/model` twice with different tuning) would print the first entry's values for both lines. Edge case. Actually wait — can a role chain legitimately contain the same ModelRef label twice? `roles: default: [openai/gpt-4o, openai/gpt-4o]`? Unusual. And both would be distinct entries only if their tuning fields differ. Marginal. Also `register` would replace per (name, baseUrl) — same name+same baseUrl+same values → one row. Same name, different baseUrl (different baseUrls for same provider/model in two chains?) → two rows, notices both resolve to the first. OK marginal but real inconsistency with the "print every seeded entry's effective values" promise. Keep as SUGGESTION.

Actually, hold on — there's a subtler version: TWO DIFFERENT entries, one named `glm-relay` (customProviders) and another whose label collides... lanes are namespaced, so no. Only within-lane same-name-different-baseUrl: customProviders names are unique (registry enforced?) — let me verify CustomProviderRegistry enforces unique names. `mergeCustomProviderEntries`... `/provider` save replaces by name. Yaml parse: could a hand-edited config declare two entries with the same name? Let me check fromYaml loop — does it dedup/error? If hand-edited yaml can carry duplicate names, then two tuning rows with the same name and different baseUrls are possible and the notice for the second shows the first's values. Let me check quickly.

💡 **SUGGESTION: `{"ref": ...}` queue entries silently ignore `connectTimeoutMs`/`streamIdleTimeoutMs` in inline `provider_config` overrides**

`ProviderQueueEntry.fromJsonMap` (the direct form) now parses the two tuning keys strictly, but the ref form bypasses it entirely: `resolvedRef` reads only `model`/`baseUrl`/`apiKeyEnv`/`contextWindow`/`maxTokens` from the `overrides` map. A ref entry with

```yaml
- ref: my-glm-provider
  provider_config:
    streamIdleTimeoutMs: 1500   # silently ignored — no parse, no error
```

gets neither the override nor a `ConfigException` — exactly the "typo silently keeps the default" failure mode this card's strict-parse philosophy exists to prevent (and AC1 claims the keys are "Parsed from … providersQueue: entries", which the ref form is).

Mitigating context: production boot (`resolveProviderQueueAtBoot`) never passes a `resolveRef` callback today, so ref entries hard-fail at boot anyway — this path is currently test-only. Also, a plain `{"ref": name}` (no inline override) still gets the referenced provider's tuning for free via the customProviders lane's URL-keyed registration, so the common case works.

Fix whenever ref resolution gets wired: parse the two keys in `resolvedRef` via the same `parseProviderTimeoutMs` (and optionally extend the `resolveRef` signature to carry the referenced entry's tuning). A test pinning the ref+override behavior would close the gap.

💡 **SUGGESTION: boot notices resolve values by `forName` (first match) — same-name entries with different baseUrls print the wrong entry's values**

`providerTuningBootNotices()` renders each entry's line via `resolveProviderTimeouts(name: entry.name)`, which is `forName` → the FIRST registry row with that name. The lanes are name-spaced (`models.custom.*`, `role:*`, `queue:*`), so cross-lane collisions are impossible, but within a lane a duplicate name is reachable: a hand-edited `customProviders:` yaml list is not deduped by name (`CliConfig.fromYaml` maps every entry), so two `name: glm-relay` rows with different `baseUrl`s/overrides register as two tuning rows — and both boot lines resolve through the first one, printing entry A's values on entry B's line. That contradicts AC1's "boot notices print every seeded entry's effective values".

The queue-lane precedence fix in r2 made `forUrl` deterministic; the notice path just needs the same treatment — e.g. resolve the values from the entry itself (`entry.connect ?? global?.connect ?? …`, or `resolveProviderTimeouts(url: Uri.parse(entry.baseUrl))` won't help for equal bases — safest is resolving per-entry fields directly) instead of re-looking up by name.

💡 **SUGGESTION: `CustomProviderEntry.toYaml()` return type widened `Map<String, String>` → `Map<String, Object?>` — note it for consumers**

Necessary change (the tuning keys are `int`s now), and no in-repo caller pins the old type. But this is a barrel-exported public API, and any external consumer that annotated the result as `Map<String, String>` stops compiling against this version. The CHANGELOG entry for this card doesn't mention the signature change — worth one clause there (or in a breaking-changes note) so hosts embedding the package aren't surprised.

blocks.text:
Found a real gap: `ProviderQueueEntry.resolvedRef` (the `{"ref": name}` queue form) resolves `model`, `baseUrl`, `apiKeyEnv`, `contextWindow`, `maxTokens` from the referenced customProviders entry — but does NOT resolve `connectTimeout`/`streamIdleTimeout` from the referenced entry, and `resolvedRef` has no parameters to receive them either (the `resolveRef` callback signature returns `({String kind, String? baseUrl, String model, String? keyName})` — it doesn't even fetch tuning fields).

Impact: a queue entry `{"ref": my-glm-provider}` where `my-glm-provider` (in customProviders:) declares `streamIdleTimeoutMs: 1500` — the queue entry is seeded via `seedProviderTuning(queueEntries:)` with `connect: null, streamIdle: null` → `ProviderTuningEntry.isEmpty` → NOT registered. So the queue lane's entry is missing from the table.

BUT — the customProviders lane also registered `my-glm-provider` with its tuning (baseUrl same as the materialized ref). So URL lookups still resolve the customProvider's entry → tuning applies. So functionally the watchdog tuning is NOT lost (the seed doc's claim "URL-keyed lookup finds the entry" is exactly this).

Is there any case where the loss matters? If the queue ref's materialized baseUrl DIFFERS from the referenced customProvider's baseUrl (inline `provider_config.baseUrl` override on the ref entry) AND the tuning was on the referenced provider → tuning lost for the overridden URL. Edge of an edge. Also: the boot notice for the customProviders entry prints regardless.

More subtle: `providerTuningBootNotices()` prints entries in the table. The ref'd queue entry itself never appears as `queue:...` — fine, the customProviders line covers it.

So: functional impact is negligible (tuning follows the baseUrl via the config lane), but there IS an inconsistency: a ref+inline-override queue entry pointing at a different baseUrl silently loses the referenced provider's tuning. Given the territory, I'd rate this a SUGGESTION (or borderline IMPORTANT). The wiring to fix it would need `resolveRef` to return tuning fields — a slightly bigger surface. Since the practical case (no baseUrl override on refs) works via the URL-keyed lookup, and the PR doc explicitly documents ref behavior ("Queue `ref` entries need no special handling — they materialize the referenced custom provider's `baseUrl`, so the URL-keyed lookup finds the entry"), the doc is honest for the common case but incomplete for the ref+baseUrl-override case. I'll file as SUGGESTION with the concrete edge case.

That's inconsistent with the strict-parse philosophy ("a typo must never silently keep the default") — a user setting `provider_config.streamIdleTimeoutMs` on a ref entry gets NOTHING: no override, no error. No injection surface. `Retry-After` rawHeader quoted into trace lines — a malicious server could inject arbitrary text into the trace (`retry-after malformed ("<server-controlled>")`). Where do trace lines render? They're part of the AC4 contract for #1395 to consume — logs/session records. A malicious/compromised provider could put a huge or control-char-laden string in Retry-After and it would land in a log line. Log injection is a classic concern but the trace isn't wired yet (#1395). The value is bounded by header size limits (typically 8KB). Low risk — could mention as part of a suggestion? The redaction layer handles secrets; a server-controlled header echoed into logs is standard practice (user agents echo URLs etc.). I'll skip or fold into the drift note. Actually — one real point: `rawHeader` in `formatRetryTraceLine` is quoted raw; when #1395 wires it, a newline in the header could forge log lines. HTTP header values can't contain raw newlines (rejected by parsers), so fine. Skip.

**Duplication**: `_humanize` lives in provider_tuning.dart — is there an existing duration humanizer in formatters.dart (trajectory formatters)? There's `formatters.dart` in trajectory with duration formatting. Potential duplication — a shared `formatDuration` might exist. Let me check.

No in-repo callers. It's a pub-package (hosted) — external consumers could break. Minor BC note — SUGGESTION. Actually wait, is it necessary? `'connectTimeoutMs': ?connectTimeout?.inMilliseconds` — int? value — so yes the map must hold ints now. The widening is necessary. The severity: source-breaking for external users of the barrel who annotated the result type. Dart semantics: return-type widening is source-compatible at call sites using `var`/`final` without explicit type, and `Map<String, Object?>` accepts all previous reads... but not reassignment into `Map<String, String>` typed variables. Minor; mention as a suggestion/BC note. Hmm — for a published package, MAJOR version discipline may apply, but this repo's CHANGELOG doesn't seem to follow semver strictly for such internal APIs. I'll note it briefly.

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: `{"ref": ...}` queue entries silently ignore `connectTimeoutMs`/`streamIdleTimeoutMs` in inline `provider_config` overrides**

`ProviderQueueEntry.fromJsonMap` (the direct form) now parses the two tuning keys strictly, but the ref form bypasses it entirely: `resolvedRef` reads only `model`/`baseUrl`/`apiKeyEnv`/`contextWindow`/`maxTokens` from the `overrides` map. A ref entry with

```yaml
- ref: my-glm-provider
  provider_config:
    streamIdleTimeoutMs: 1500   # silently ignored — no parse, no error
```

gets neither the override nor a `ConfigException` — exactly the "typo silently keeps the default" failure mode this card's strict-parse philosophy exists to prevent (and AC1 claims the keys are "Parsed from … providersQueue: entries", which the ref form is).

Mitigating context: production boot (`resolveProviderQueueAtBoot`) never passes a `resolveRef` callback today, so ref entries hard-fail at boot anyway — this path is currently test-only. Also, a plain `{"ref": name}` (no inline override) still gets the referenced provider's tuning for free via the customProviders lane's URL-keyed registration, so the common case works.

Fix whenever ref resolution gets wired: parse the two keys in `resolvedRef` via the same `parseProviderTimeoutMs` (and optionally extend the `resolveRef` signature to carry the referenced entry's tuning). A test pinning the ref+override behavior would close the gap.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md"}

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: boot notices resolve values by `forName` (first match) — same-name entries with different baseUrls print the wrong entry's values**

`providerTuningBootNotices()` renders each entry's line via `resolveProviderTimeouts(name: entry.name)`, which is `forName` → the FIRST registry row with that name. The lanes are name-spaced (`models.custom.*`, `role:*`, `queue:*`), so cross-lane collisions are impossible, but within a lane a duplicate name is reachable: a hand-edited `customProviders:` yaml list is not deduped by name (`CliConfig.fromYaml` maps every entry), so two `name: glm-relay` rows with different `baseUrl`s/overrides register as two tuning rows — and both boot lines resolve through the first one, printing entry A's values on entry B's line. That contradicts AC1's "boot notices print every seeded entry's effective values".

The queue-lane precedence fix in r2 made `forUrl` deterministic; the notice path just needs the same treatment — e.g. resolve the values from the entry itself (`entry.connect ?? global?.connect ?? …`, or `resolveProviderTimeouts(url: Uri.parse(entry.baseUrl))` won't help for equal bases — safest is resolving per-entry fields directly) instead of re-looking up by name.

No injection surface. `Retry-After` rawHeader quoted into trace lines — a malicious server could inject arbitrary text into the trace (`retry-after malformed ("<server-controlled>")`). Where do trace lines render? They're part of the AC4 contract for #1395 to consume — logs/session records. A malicious/compromised provider could put a huge or control-char-laden string in Retry-After and it would land in a log line. Log injection is a classic concern but the trace isn't wired yet (#1395). The value is bounded by header size limits (typically 8KB). Low risk — could mention as part of a suggestion? The redaction layer handles secrets; a server-controlled header echoed into logs is standard practice (user agents echo URLs etc.). I'll skip or fold into the drift note. Actually — one real point: `rawHeader` in `formatRetryTraceLine` is quoted raw; when #1395 wires it, a newline in the header could forge log lines. HTTP header values can't contain raw newlines (rejected by parsers), so fine. Skip.

**Duplication**: `_humanize` lives in provider_tuning.dart — is there an existing duration humanizer in formatters.dart (trajectory formatters)? There's `formatters.dart` in trajectory with duration formatting. Potential duplication — a shared `formatDuration` might exist. Let me check.

No in-repo callers. It's a pub-package (hosted) — external consumers could break. Minor BC note — SUGGESTION. Actually wait, is it necessary? `'connectTimeoutMs': ?connectTimeout?.inMilliseconds` — int? value — so yes the map must hold ints now. The widening is necessary. The severity: source-breaking for external users of the barrel who annotated the result type. Dart semantics: return-type widening is source-compatible at call sites using `var`/`final` without explicit type, and `Map<String, Object?>` accepts all previous reads... but not reassignment into `Map<String, String>` typed variables. Minor; mention as a suggestion/BC note. Hmm — for a published package, MAJOR version discipline may apply, but this repo's CHANGELOG doesn't seem to follow semver strictly for such internal APIs. I'll note it briefly.

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: `{"ref": ...}` queue entries silently ignore `connectTimeoutMs`/`streamIdleTimeoutMs` in inline `provider_config` overrides**

`ProviderQueueEntry.fromJsonMap` (the direct form) now parses the two tuning keys strictly, but the ref form bypasses it entirely: `resolvedRef` reads only `model`/`baseUrl`/`apiKeyEnv`/`contextWindow`/`maxTokens` from the `overrides` map. A ref entry with

```yaml
- ref: my-glm-provider
  provider_config:
    streamIdleTimeoutMs: 1500   # silently ignored — no parse, no error
```

gets neither the override nor a `ConfigException` — exactly the "typo silently keeps the default" failure mode this card's strict-parse philosophy exists to prevent (and AC1 claims the keys are "Parsed from … providersQueue: entries", which the ref form is).

Mitigating context: production boot (`resolveProviderQueueAtBoot`) never passes a `resolveRef` callback today, so ref entries hard-fail at boot anyway — this path is currently test-only. Also, a plain `{"ref": name}` (no inline override) still gets the referenced provider's tuning for free via the customProviders lane's URL-keyed registration, so the common case works.

Fix whenever ref resolution gets wired: parse the two keys in `resolvedRef` via the same `parseProviderTimeoutMs` (and optionally extend the `resolveRef` signature to carry the referenced entry's tuning). A test pinning the ref+override behavior would close the gap.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md"}

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: boot notices resolve values by `forName` (first match) — same-name entries with different baseUrls print the wrong entry's values**

`providerTuningBootNotices()` renders each entry's line via `resolveProviderTimeouts(name: entry.name)`, which is `forName` → the FIRST registry row with that name. The lanes are name-spaced (`models.custom.*`, `role:*`, `queue:*`), so cross-lane collisions are impossible, but within a lane a duplicate name is reachable: a hand-edited `customProviders:` yaml list is not deduped by name (`CliConfig.fromYaml` maps every entry), so two `name: glm-relay` rows with different `baseUrl`s/overrides register as two tuning rows — and both boot lines resolve through the first one, printing entry A's values on entry B's line. That contradicts AC1's "boot notices print every seeded entry's effective values".

The queue-lane precedence fix in r2 made `forUrl` deterministic; the notice path just needs the same treatment — e.g. resolve the values from the entry itself (`entry.connect ?? global?.connect ?? …`, or `resolveProviderTimeouts(url: Uri.parse(entry.baseUrl))` won't help for equal bases — safest is resolving per-entry fields directly) instead of re-looking up by name.

All correct. Now let me do the exhaustive second pass on the remaining dimensions while gates run:

**Security**: No secrets in the new code — tuning values are durations; boot notices print name+baseUrl+durations (baseUrl was already printed elsewhere; the model line prints provider). `parseProviderTimeoutMs` error messages include the raw value — could echo a config value, but that's standard for config errors. No injection surface. `Retry-After` rawHeader quoted into trace lines — a malicious server could inject arbitrary text into the trace (`retry-after malformed ("<server-controlled>")`). Where do trace lines render? They're part of the AC4 contract for #1395 to consume — logs/session records. A malicious/compromised provider could put a huge or control-char-laden string in Retry-After and it would land in a log line. Log injection is a classic concern but the trace isn't wired yet (#1395). The value is bounded by header size limits (typically 8KB). Low risk — could mention as part of a suggestion? The redaction layer handles secrets; a server-controlled header echoed into logs is standard practice (user agents echo URLs etc.). I'll skip or fold into the drift note. Actually — one real point: `rawHeader` in `formatRetryTraceLine` is quoted raw; when #1395 wires it, a newline in the header could forge log lines. HTTP header values can't contain raw newlines (rejected by parsers), so fine. Skip.

**Duplication**: `_humanize` lives in provider_tuning.dart — is there an existing duration humanizer in formatters.dart (trajectory formatters)? There's `formatters.dart` in trajectory with duration formatting. Potential duplication — a shared `formatDuration` might exist. Let me check.

**Backward compat**: `CustomProviderEntry.toYaml()` return-type widening `Map<String, String>` → `Map<String, Object?>`. Assignments of the result to `Map<String, String>` would break. No in-repo callers. It's a pub-package (hosted) — external consumers could break. Minor BC note — SUGGESTION. Actually wait, is it necessary? `'connectTimeoutMs': ?connectTimeout?.inMilliseconds` — int? value — so yes the map must hold ints now. The widening is necessary. The severity: source-breaking for external users of the barrel who annotated the result type. Dart semantics: return-type widening is source-compatible at call sites using `var`/`final` without explicit type, and `Map<String, Object?>` accepts all previous reads... but not reassignment into `Map<String, String>` typed variables. Minor; mention as a suggestion/BC note. Hmm — for a published package, MAJOR version discipline may apply, but this repo's CHANGELOG doesn't seem to follow semver strictly for such internal APIs. I'll note it briefly.

**ProviderQueueEntry constructor** — new named params added; `const`? It has a body (kind check) so not const. Fine.

**Error paths**: parse errors name field+entry ✔.

**The remaining findings so far:**
1. SUGGESTION: `resolvedRef` (queue `{"ref": ...}` + inline `provider_config`) silently ignores `connectTimeoutMs`/`streamIdleTimeoutMs` — inconsistent with the strict-parse philosophy; currently test-only path (production boot never passes resolveRef), so consistency fix can ride whenever ref resolution gets wired.

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: `{"ref": ...}` queue entries silently ignore `connectTimeoutMs`/`streamIdleTimeoutMs` in inline `provider_config` overrides**

`ProviderQueueEntry.fromJsonMap` (the direct form) now parses the two tuning keys strictly, but the ref form bypasses it entirely: `resolvedRef` reads only `model`/`baseUrl`/`apiKeyEnv`/`contextWindow`/`maxTokens` from the `overrides` map. A ref entry with

```yaml
- ref: my-glm-provider
  provider_config:
    streamIdleTimeoutMs: 1500   # silently ignored — no parse, no error
```

gets neither the override nor a `ConfigException` — exactly the "typo silently keeps the default" failure mode this card's strict-parse philosophy exists to prevent (and AC1 claims the keys are "Parsed from … providersQueue: entries", which the ref form is).

Mitigating context: production boot (`resolveProviderQueueAtBoot`) never passes a `resolveRef` callback today, so ref entries hard-fail at boot anyway — this path is currently test-only. Also, a plain `{"ref": name}` (no inline override) still gets the referenced provider's tuning for free via the customProviders lane's URL-keyed registration, so the common case works.

Fix whenever ref resolution gets wired: parse the two keys in `resolvedRef` via the same `parseProviderTimeoutMs` (and optionally extend the `resolveRef` signature to carry the referenced entry's tuning). A test pinning the ref+override behavior would close the gap.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md"}

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: boot notices resolve values by `forName` (first match) — same-name entries with different baseUrls print the wrong entry's values**

`providerTuningBootNotices()` renders each entry's line via `resolveProviderTimeouts(name: entry.name)`, which is `forName` → the FIRST registry row with that name. The lanes are name-spaced (`models.custom.*`, `role:*`, `queue:*`), so cross-lane collisions are impossible, but within a lane a duplicate name is reachable: a hand-edited `customProviders:` yaml list is not deduped by name (`CliConfig.fromYaml` maps every entry), so two `name: glm-relay` rows with different `baseUrl`s/overrides register as two tuning rows — and both boot lines resolve through the first one, printing entry A's values on entry B's line. That contradicts AC1's "boot notices print every seeded entry's effective values".

The queue-lane precedence fix in r2 made `forUrl` deterministic; the notice path just needs the same treatment — e.g. resolve the values from the entry itself (`entry.connect ?? global?.connect ?? …`, or `resolveProviderTimeouts(url: Uri.parse(entry.baseUrl))` won't help for equal bases — safest is resolving per-entry fields directly) instead of re-looking up by name.
